a230.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a230.name: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo
a230.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a230.speech: Words addressed by the Head of Government to the wounded soldiers: "I have come to inquire about your state of health and to wish you a speedy recovery. I have come to express to you our admiration for your spirit of sacrifice which allows our country to remain standing."

a230.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a230.name: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouedraogo
a230.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a230.speech: Declared to the medical staff: "I thank you for all the efforts you are making to care for our wounded soldiers. I salute your individual and collective commitment, despite the difficult working conditions. When one looks at the state of the wounded and above all the quality of the care they receive, which today allows us to hope that they may recover their health, one can only salute you. It is a state of mind that the Government salutes. Everything is being done to improve your working conditions. Continue to perform miracles."

a234.speaker: Jeremiah K. Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a234.name: Jeremiah K. Koung
a234.title: Vice President of Liberia
a234.speech: Officially breaking ground for the project, along with the deed signing and turning over on behalf of President Joseph N. Boakai, extended appreciation and gratitude to Liberia's Special Economic Zone Authority and partners for the initiative, while extending President Boakai's sincere apologies for his absence; according to VP Koung, the initiative is a key part of President Boakai's ARREST Agenda, focusing on Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation, and Tourism, while reflecting that fifty years ago, former President William R. Tolbert, Jr. gave birth to this vision, but fifty years on, Liberia has done nothing about achieving this.

a234.speaker: Jeremiah K. Koung, Vice President of Liberia
a234.name: Jeremiah K. Koung
a234.title: Vice President of Liberia
a234.speech: Urged the partners and contractors to recruit community dwellers to help on the project implementation, adding that such will give ownership to the residents and provide domestic security, while urging local residents to make use of the community college to prepare themselves for opportunities ahead. "Now, President Boakai, who understands what it means when it comes to agriculture and value addition, has decided to bring this dream to reality. Now, we urge that you increase your speed. If you were running at sixty, double at one twenty. Our people can't wait. If you have any issues and want anything to move, come to me and I will meet the President. Our people want this because they provided the land. When the deed is prepared today, you can build all the roads, but if the bread and butter issues are not addressed, the people will still have problems. Let me inform you that this is what is going to address the bread and butter issues. This project is the President's baby and he wants to see it come to fulfillment", the Vice President explained.

a234.speaker: Kaustella Kialain Sarsih, AfDB Senior Transport Engineer (on behalf of the African Development Bank)
a234.name: Kaustella Kialain Sarsih
a234.title: AfDB Senior Transport Engineer (on behalf of the African Development Bank)
a234.speech: Reaffirmed the Bank's commitment, while disclosing that Liberia joins other West African countries like Nigeria, Guinea, Senegal, and Togo in this agro-industrial effort. "I am deeply honored to represent the AfDB. Today's groundbreaking and deed signing for Liberia's first Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zone (SAPZ) is far more than a ceremonial program. It's an action that indicates that agro-business is the next step for national prosperity. The AfDB stands strongly shoulder to shoulder with the Government of Liberia to achieve this. With US$16m from the Bank already approved and further US$13m, we reaffirmed our commitment to support Liberia", she stated.

a234.speaker: Thomas Alexander Goshua, Grand Bassa County District #5 Representative
a234.name: Thomas Alexander Goshua
a234.title: Grand Bassa County District #5 Representative
a234.speech: Extolled and appreciated the government for its commitment to rural development, and agriculture development. "I want to thank President Boakai and the Vice President, who is currently here, for the initiative. We've long been saying that things will happen in Bassa and it will be good for us and everyone of us will enjoy. For a very long time, people have been telling us that the Bassa people gave their land for smoked fish. This time, we are not giving it for smoked fish but for development and improvement. So, I want to appreciate the people of Bassa district #5 for agreeing with us to provide this land to do this initiative", Representative Goshua stated.

a234.speaker: Prince Redd, Executive Chairperson of the Liberia Special Economic Zones Authority (LSEZA)
a234.name: Prince Redd
a234.title: Executive Chairperson of the Liberia Special Economic Zones Authority (LSEZA)
a234.speech: Providing an overview and background of the project, described the US$19.4 million project as a pivotal moment for advancing value-added agriculture, economic growth, and job creation; according to him, the project is the dawn of an economic Zone for Grand Bassa and a mark of a responsible government, while appreciating the hospitable people of Grand Bassa County for providing the land to address food insecurity and job creation. "Today, we are not just breaking ground, we are breaking limits. Mr. Vice President, kindly extend to the President that we at the LSEZA are proud to be the regulating body in the Liberia circular and Economic Zone. We also want to appreciate our partners, the African Development Bank, whose funding made this possible. Also, USAID for supporting the foundational feasibility study, World Bank, among others", Mr. Redd said.

a234.speaker: Liberian government officials
a234.name: Liberian government officials
a234.speech: The government views agricultural transformation as central to Liberia's economic recovery, with officials describing farming as "the heartbeat" of the President's development agenda.

a255.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a255.name: Donald Trump
a255.title: US President
a255.speech: Promised "hell" for the Palestinian Islamist movement if it did not release "all the hostages" by Saturday ; described Hamas's threat to postpone the releases as "terrible" ; "If all the hostages are not brought back by Saturday midday (...) I would say: cancel it (the truce agreement) and all bets are off, let all hell break loose," he told the press.

a255.speaker: Hamas
a255.name: Hamas
a255.speech: Responded to the American president by stating that "the language of threats is worthless and only complicates matters".

a255.speaker: Hamas
a255.name: Hamas
a255.speech: Threatened on Monday to postpone the next hostage release scheduled for Saturday under the truce agreement, accusing Israel of violating it, and asserted that "the door remains open" for a release on Saturday if Israel "fulfils its obligations".

a255.speaker: Sami Abou Zouhri, a leader of Hamas
a255.name: Sami Abou Zouhri
a255.title: a leader of Hamas
a255.speech: "Trump must remember that there is an agreement (a truce) which must be respected by both parties (Israel and Hamas) and that this is the only way to bring the prisoners back."

a255.speaker: Head of the United Nations (UN Secretary-General)
a255.name: Head of the United Nations (UN Secretary-General)
a255.speech: Called on Hamas to continue releasing the hostages: "We must avoid at all costs a resumption of hostilities in Gaza which would lead to an immense tragedy."

a255.speaker: Government of Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a255.name: Government of Benjamin Netanyahu
a255.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a255.speech: Immediately ordered its army to prepare for "all scenarios" and sent reinforcements around the Gaza Strip.

a255.speaker: Israeli army
a255.name: Israeli army
a255.speech: According to the army, at least 35 of the 73 hostages still held in Gaza are dead.

a255.speaker: Israeli army and the Kibbutz of Kissufim
a255.name: Israeli army and the Kibbutz of Kissufim
a255.speech: Announced on Tuesday the death in captivity in Gaza of Shlomo Mansour, 86, seized from his home in the kibbutz during the Hamas attack.

a255.speaker: AFP tally based on official Israeli figures
a255.name: AFP tally based on official Israeli figures
a255.speech: The 7 October attack led to the deaths of 1,210 people on the Israeli side, mostly civilians.

a255.speaker: Hamas Health Ministry (data, considered reliable by the UN)
a255.name: Hamas Health Ministry (data
a255.title: considered reliable by the UN)
a255.speech: The Israeli offensive has killed at least 48,208 people, mostly civilians, in Gaza and caused colossal destruction and a humanitarian disaster.

a255.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a255.name: Donald Trump
a255.title: US President
a255.speech: Asserted, while receiving Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington last week, that the United States would take "control" of Gaza in order to rebuild it and develop it economically, proposing to displace Gazans notably to Jordan or Egypt ; in an interview with Fox News he then asserted that the Palestinians would no longer be able to return to Gaza because "they will have much better housing".

a255.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a255.name: Donald Trump
a255.title: US President
a255.speech: Warned on Monday that he was considering halting aid to Egypt and Jordan if they did not take in the Palestinians.

a674.speaker: Kalidbomba (Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency)
a674.name: Kalidbomba (Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency)
a674.speech: "Even if nutrition is a clear human health issue it also has a direct relationship with the farmers and the agriculture directly." ; "The success of the hotline in this short period of time is derived by the high demand of the farmers to access helpful information."

a674.speaker: Ekin Ogutogullari, Country Director of Save the Children in Ethiopia
a674.name: Ekin Ogutogullari
a674.title: Country Director of Save the Children in Ethiopia
a674.speech: "It is a smart and timely information dissemination tool which is enabled by this partnership with ATA." ; "It helps us avoid duplication of efforts and wisely use available resources and it will contribute to the dietary consumption behavior improvement of farmers."

a777.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a777.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a777.speech: Called for redoubling efforts at all levels in order to achieve the eradication of malaria provided for in the document adopted by the WHO in May 2015, entitled Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016-2030.

a777.speaker: WHO report (published December 2024)
a777.name: WHO report (published December 2024)
a777.speech: "The African region is the most affected by malaria, accounting for about 94% of global cases and 95% of malaria-related deaths in 2023. Slightly more than half of these deaths occurred in four countries: Nigeria (30.9%), the Democratic Republic of Congo (11.3%), Niger (5.9%) and the United Republic of Tanzania (4.3%)" ; the most recent WHO figures, dating from 2023, report a toll of 597,000 deaths from the disease.

a777.speaker: James Tibenderana, Director General of the British NGO Malaria Consortium (quoted by Le Monde)
a777.name: James Tibenderana
a777.title: Director General of the British NGO Malaria Consortium (quoted by Le Monde)
a777.speech: Declared: "There are fears that it may not be able to start on time in some West African countries where we operate, when the rains begin in June-July."

a777.speaker: Dorothy Achu, head of the malaria and tropical diseases team at the WHO Africa office
a777.name: Dorothy Achu
a777.title: head of the malaria and tropical diseases team at the WHO Africa office
a777.speech: Warned that "malaria can be treated, but in young children this disease quickly becomes fatal when treatment is delayed."

a777.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a777.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a777.speech: According to the WHO, a growing number of countries have made the fight against and elimination of malaria a national priority; no fewer than 11 high-burden African countries had signed the Yaounde Declaration in March 2024.

a777.speaker: Dr Daniel Ngamije, Director of the WHO Global Malaria Programme
a777.name: Dr Daniel Ngamije
a777.title: Director of the WHO Global Malaria Programme
a777.speech: Declared: "The ministers committed to strengthening their health systems, increasing domestic resources, reinforcing multisectoral action and guaranteeing a robust accountability mechanism" ; "this is the kind of leadership the world must rally behind."

a823.speaker: Swapo Party branch, Walvis Bay
a823.name: Swapo Party branch
a823.title: Walvis Bay
a823.speech: Has dismissed allegations that its district office was involved in compiling or managing the list of beneficiaries for the Farm 37 housing project.

a823.speaker: Inge Zaamwani, Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform
a823.name: Inge Zaamwani
a823.title: Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Land Reform
a823.speech: Has confirmed that disciplinary action was taken against the Agro-Marketing and Trade Agency’s (AMTA’s) former Managing Director and its former senior manager for Finance and Logistics after employees unduly benefited from the company’s finances.

a823.speaker: Vipuakuje Muharukua, Kunene Regional Governor
a823.name: Vipuakuje Muharukua
a823.title: Kunene Regional Governor
a823.speech: Has stated that the planned State of the Region address will proceed as scheduled, despite what he describes as attempts to undermine his constitutional responsibility to address the council and the Kunene Region.

a823.speaker: Minister of Urban and Rural Development
a823.name: Minister of Urban and Rural Development
a823.speech: Has raised concerns about poor financial management and weak governance in some regional councils and local authorities.

a823.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a823.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a823.title: President of Namibia
a823.speech: Has stated that the government is dedicated to ensuring that those responsible for the shooting and throwing of acid at Justine Shiweda will be brought to justice.

a823.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of Namibia
a823.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a823.title: President of Namibia
a823.speech: Has questioned the Ministry of Agriculture’s decision to retain management of the Kalimbeza National Rice Project, instead of transferring it to the University of Namibia (UNAM) as she previously recommended.

a823.speaker: Natalia |Goagoses, Governor of the Erongo Region
a823.name: Natalia |Goagoses
a823.title: Governor of the Erongo Region
a823.speech: Said Namibians should dismantle the architecture of fraud and corruption by constructing a future of transparency, integrity and shared prosperity.

a823.speaker: Residents from Arandis, Walvis Bay and Swakopmund
a823.name: Residents from Arandis
a823.title: Walvis Bay and Swakopmund
a823.speech: Demand urgent action against what they describe as widespread corruption and mismanagement at the Erongo Regional Council.

a932.speaker: Marcus Low, editor of Spotlight, and Nathan Geffen, editor of GroundUp (analysis column)
a932.name: Marcus Low
a932.title: editor of Spotlight, and Nathan Geffen, editor of GroundUp (analysis column)
a932.speech: Write that the sudden and severe US cuts to grants from the world's largest health research funder threaten to unravel the medical research landscape in South Africa, and that a crucial question now is whether the government will turn this crisis into an opportunity for renewal; argue that some kind of bailout is clearly needed to avert the loss of so much human capital, suggesting the SAMRC be allocated an extra R1 billion per year to keep at least some clinical trials and other research efforts on track.

a932.speaker: Spotlight (analysis published earlier this month)
a932.name: Spotlight (analysis published earlier this month)
a932.speech: Estimated that every year about R800 million in NIH grants goes to studies where South African researchers are the primary investigators.

a932.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, previous head of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a932.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a932.title: previous head of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a932.speech: Has been quoted saying as much as $250 million (about R4.5 billion) per year might be lost to medical research in South Africa.

a932.speaker: South African government
a932.name: South African government
a932.speech: Has previously committed to spend 1.5% of GDP on R&D by 2030 - at last count the country was below 1%.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Opened by giving thanks to God and thanking the Head of State, the President of the CNSP and the Prime Minister for placing their confidence in him to manage a strategic ministry, "because food sovereignty is a priority", and thanked the RTN for the opportunity to present 18 months of management to citizens, offering the population his best wishes for 2025, "so that we may truly have a year of peace and stability".

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Recalled the context of Niger after 26 July 2023, which he said must remain in the collective memory of Nigeriens: "The first act after 26 July 2023: ECOWAS took inhuman, unjust measures, notably the closing of the borders and the blockades of Niger's territory." He said there was a real threat of military attack on Niger, with some announcing thousands of men and aircraft having overflown Niger; that all the country's financial resources were blocked by the BCEAO; and that Niger had no possibility of importing pharmaceutical or food products, with goods that had already left the port of Cotonou for Gaya prevented from entering Niger.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said that Niger imports practically all the cereals needed to feed its roughly 27 million inhabitants - rice, wheat, maize and even millet - and that 2023 was a deficit year, with an agricultural deficit of nearly 955,000 tonnes and a fodder deficit of nearly 54 per cent (exactly 53.8 per cent), so that the combined security and food-security challenges had to be met very quickly.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said Niger has always had good relations with Togo and Burkina Faso, which told the CNSP and the government they were ready to accompany Niger, and thanked the Togolese and Burkinabe peoples for that support, which "must also remain in the collective memory of Nigeriens"; he said the corridor question had to be settled to supply the country, that a whole machine was put in place and that more than 2,000 soldiers were mobilised to escort food convoys and resupply Niger very quickly.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Explained that a range of actions was launched on the basis of the Head of State's vision, whose third axis concerns agriculture, with a mission letter of 7 essential points and an agricultural policy comprising three programmes: development of plant production, development of animal production, and support to institutions and monitoring of the ministry's action.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said Niger has some 62 million head of livestock of all species, great potential of irrigable land and potential in ground and surface water (the Niger river, the Komadougou, the Korama, the Maggia) over 1,267,000 km2, and that since cereals cannot be grown reliably under rainfall on 60 to 70 per cent of the territory, the Grande Irrigation Programme was developed: "God has given us a potential that cannot be taken away: the sun, the water, the land. We have everything needed to produce."

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: On the Grande Irrigation Programme, said that of the 18,500 hectares of hydro-agricultural developments under ONAHA's control barely 8,500 hectares are genuinely farmed in double season, which he called "a catastrophe" for a Sahelian country from 1960 to 26 July; that the first action is to rehabilitate the roughly 10,000 hectares practically out of use; that Niger needs about 700,000 tonnes of rice a year, requiring at least 40,000 hectares in double season (80,000 hectares), so 21,200 additional hectares must be developed to cover 50 per cent of rice needs (about 315,000 tonnes) plus maize and wheat; the programme therefore consists of rehabilitating and developing at least 39,700 hectares.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said that under embargo the Head of State's instructions were to proceed on the country's own internal resources, that a multi-year contract plan was signed with ONAHA running to 2027 to rehabilitate 2,000 hectares and develop 2,000 new hectares each year, and that the flagship PACIPA project and other supervised projects would take the remainder. On results, he said the Grande Irrigation Programme was launched in March 2024 from Niamey and rolled out in all regions: 160 hectares with a dyke at Diffa ("had it not been for the floods, Diffa would today be supplying rice nearly everywhere"), the Kassama irrigated perimeter whose rice is now on the market, the Jambali development at Maradi with 160 hectares, and the 32 km Dolle Kagatawey dyke which secured 3,000 hectares of rice unexploited for almost five years; launches also took place at Niamey, Toulla (Tillaberi), Tiguirwit (Agadez) and Moulela (Tahoua). "Some of the 13 perimeters I have just listed are practically finished, others are pending and soon we will take delivery of them." He put spending from own resources at about 23 billion so far, adding "rice will soon be on the market".

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: On Niamey, replied "It would surprise me, Abdoulaye, that you say it is slow to start. If you had been to Saguia you would not say that," and said two things must not be confused: existing developments being rehabilitated, and the fact that Niamey has no additional space to build new developments. He said the issue is production basins rather than regions - "if we can produce rice in Maradi for the needs of the whole of Niger, we will do so" - and that the necessary technical arrangements, roads and transport would be put in place; asked to acknowledge that Niamey's existing perimeters function rather badly, he answered "Unfortunately! That is precisely why the Grande Irrigation Programme exists," pledging to rehabilitate all 10,000 non-functional hectares of the 18,500 existing.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said that for a long time it was thought rice could only be produced where there is permanent water such as rivers, but it has been realised that it can be produced even in lowlands and outside developed schemes - indeed the largest quantity comes from there, as in the Magaria department of the Zinder region - so these prejudices must be abandoned; he said about 40,000 hectares have been made available by communes, departments and regions, and asked "let us make an appointment for 2027", preferring that the facts speak for themselves. Asked whether Niger would no longer import rice from 2027, he replied: "Let us wait and see."

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Said his mission letter charges him with sensitising citizens and conveying the messages of the government and the CNSP, which is why he has visited the whole of Niger to explain Niger's path on sovereignty, the reasons for the events of 26 July and what the government intends to bring, including on security, acting as spokesman while the security ministers were preoccupied. "What I take away is that the Nigerien people are a brave, courageous and resilient people." On his last mission to Iferouane he found men and women standing; he said Nigeriens in the most remote areas have already heard the message and expect action from the government: "It is true the context is difficult, but we will hold on."

a1070.speaker: Residents (women and men) of Iferouane, quoted by the Minister
a1070.name: Residents (women and men) of Iferouane
a1070.title: quoted by the Minister
a1070.speech: "Minister, what have we done to the CNSP - for two years we have been waiting for the arrival of a member of the government?"

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: On fertiliser, said Niger holds a little under 3 per cent of potential world phosphate reserves and a little under 40 per cent of sub-Saharan Africa's phosphate potential yet does not have a single grain of phosphate, "because we were not sovereign, because we do not decide for ourselves what we want; we were guided in our political and economic decisions"; he said sovereignty - the CNSP President's vision, "labou sanni no" or "zance kassa" - is not a slogan but a vision. He said he was instructed by the Head of State and the Prime Minister to approach the Office Cherifien des Phosphates, that a convention was signed and financing through the PACIPA project is practically secured, and that a fertiliser factory producing blends adapted to Niger's different soils will be created, replacing the three imported fertilisers (NPK 15-15, urea and DAP), with the fertiliser problem to be solved by 2027.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: On CAIMA, said "CAIMA was a catastrophe, it does not exist", and that at one point, in the framework of reforms and again as a question of sovereignty, "Germany and the United States wrested away CAIMA's ability to import and market fertiliser in order to privatise it", which was not bad in itself if the principles were followed; he argued the State must be present in the strategic fertiliser sector, said an ordinance signed 72 hours earlier restored CAIMA's full powers, and revealed that CAIMA formerly imported some 400,000-450,000 tonnes of fertiliser subsidised at 50 per cent, selling a 50 kg bag at 13,500 CFA francs when the unsubsidised market price was at most 15,000 CFA francs - "the State was cheated, our poor peasants were cheated". He said discussions were held with partners who respect Niger's sovereignty, notably India and China, to build an agricultural equipment assembly plant (tractors, threshers) in Niger, and that a new director general, Issoufou Bah, "a man of integrity", has been appointed to carry out the reform.

a1070.speaker: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman, Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.name: Colonel Elhadj Ousmane Mahaman
a1070.title: Niger's Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a1070.speech: Asked whether CAIMA would no longer be a cash cow for politicians, replied: "That is very clear... in any case we will insist on good governance," citing the first axis of the Head of State's 'Vision' book - governance - and saying good governance must reign in state structures so that the missions defined by the legislator can truly be applied.

a1070.speaker: General of Brigade Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the CNSP
a1070.name: General of Brigade Abdourahamane Tiani
a1070.title: President of the CNSP
a1070.speech: As recalled by the Minister, announced on television, at the head of his men, that the CNSP had taken power for the sovereignty of Niger.

a1070.speaker: Governments of Togo and Burkina Faso
a1070.name: Governments of Togo and Burkina Faso
a1070.speech: Told the CNSP and the Government that they were ready to accompany Niger, and responded favourably on the question of the corridors for supplying the country.

a1070.speaker: Director General of ONAHA (cited by the RTN interviewer)
a1070.name: Director General of ONAHA (cited by the RTN interviewer)
a1070.speech: Spoke of the difficulties they have in the Niamey region because there is practically no space in Niamey.

a1096.speaker: Nouhoum Maïga, Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross, and Emmanuel Lippolis, International Red Cross
a1096.name: Nouhoum Maïga
a1096.title: Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross, and Emmanuel Lippolis, International Red Cross
a1096.speech: Presented their assessment of the year 2024 in Mali at a press café: "The objectives were achieved, even exceeded," they indicated ; "The 2024 results are satisfactory, the objectives were achieved and even exceeded," the two officials underlined, while expressing reservations about the prospects for 2025, one of the main reasons for those reservations being the suspension of USAID activities and other American funds by US President Donald Trump around the world.

a1096.speaker: Nouhoum Maïga, Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross
a1096.name: Nouhoum Maïga
a1096.title: Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross
a1096.speech: Said that from December to now, in two or three months, the Malian Red Cross was able to mobilise a little more than 2 billion CFA francs out of the 5 billion expected, i.e. more than 40 per cent in only two or three months, unlike the previous appeal which over two years, "we had only been able to mobilise 18 per cent," he confided, to demonstrate the organisation's progress and feat in resource mobilisation, adding: "Last weekend, quite recently, the Red Cross launched the operations linked to the emergency appeal for relief against the humanitarian crisis in Mali."

a1096.speaker: Nouhoum Maïga, Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross
a1096.name: Nouhoum Maïga
a1096.title: Secretary General of the Malian Red Cross
a1096.speech: "As regards USAID, I don't think there is any organisation that is not impacted, either directly or by knock-on effect, by this suspension," he acknowledged ; "We are impacted but we hope that it will not last over time," hoped the Secretary General, especially concerning the release of funds intended for life-saving activities.

a1096.speaker: Emmanuel Lippolis, International Red Cross
a1096.name: Emmanuel Lippolis
a1096.title: International Red Cross
a1096.speech: Warned that if the suspension of American participation is definitive, it will be a matter, for the Red Cross, of suspending what can be suspended or slowing down what can be slowed down and continuing with all the rest; the repercussion will be there and could lead the organisation to reduce its ambitions and probably to revise downwards next year's budget.

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC)
a1388.speech: "Heading the SAMRC was definitely the best job of my life." ; "But I am excited about my future, it's time for another best job. After 10 years of doing science administration, it's time to get back and do the science."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On investment in research: says that while South Africa's health department has competing priorities, ideally it should double or triple its allocation to research. "We spend a lot of time trying to show the Department of Health how important science is. And so while there is commitment from them, they're so busy worrying about services; healthcare workers, doctors, hospitals falling down, no equipment, no cancer treatment. And so, sometimes science is seen as esoteric and a luxury." ; "Science gives you evidence to reduce morbidity and mortality. All the things that change people's lives; like Covid vaccines, ARVs, mother to child transmission interventions, typically these stem from research. And so, you can only improve outcomes if you fund research. Currently, the SAMRC gets around R750 million from government a year; in my view, around R2 billion to R3 billion a year is needed to really make profound investments in research."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: Rejects the suggestion that international donor funding means local research ends up pandering to agendas set abroad. "We (the SAMRC) always fund the 10 most common causes of mortality and morbidity in South Africa. So the funders who work with us have to agree on funding what we deem our priorities."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On transformation: "So I spent 10 years of my life changing who we funded, where we funded, how we funded; changing the demographics of the SAMRC, creating an executive management committee that was diverse, and being able to attract a great black scientist (Professor Ntobeko Ntusi) to take over from me."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On the intersection between politics and science: "As the president of the MRC, you have to be very brave and you have to be able to speak truth to power. Sometimes it's hard, and sometimes it's easy." ; "The relationship has to be flexible. Because, sometimes scientists are wrong and politicians are right. Sometimes politicians are wrong and scientists are right. And sometimes both are wrong, and sometimes both are right. And our egos can get in the way. You know: 'Oh, you took me off the MAC (Ministerial Advisory Committee), now I'm not going to help you.' That's not the right attitude to have…"

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On the Covid-19 lockdown: criticised government's lockdown regulations as "unscientific"; she said the hard lockdown was causing unemployment and unnecessary hardship and malnourishment in poor families, and later spoke out against government's continuation of restrictions on school going, the sale of certain foods and clothes like open-toe footwear, and the limits on outdoor exercise. "It's almost as if someone is sucking regulations out of their thumb and implementing rubbish, quite frankly."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On the February 2021 vaccine procurement: says she was approached by Mkhize about an alternative vaccine, to which she responded by facilitating the procurement of 500 000 doses of the Johnson & Johnson vaccine through personal connections. "The vaccines arrived in Johannesburg at about midnight." ; "Then the plane with the president's vaccine touched down in Cape Town at 12:20; and we had to rush it to Khayelitsha to have him vaccinated at one o'clock."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On her altercation with former health minister Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma in a bathroom in the late 1990s: "Thabo Mbeki had a national AIDS plan and they were about to publish it. So there was a meeting; we were presenting, and we had data that mother to child transmission interventions were affordable, or that it was actually cheaper to give ARVs to a pregnant woman, than to treat a child who is HIV positive." ; "But they kept on saying it was unaffordable, and that they wouldn't be doing it. And then, when I saw Dlamini-Zuma in the bathroom, I got into a fight with her and said: 'But it is affordable!'"

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On her childhood and early career: says they grew up poor. "My parents would often run out of money in the middle of the month, having to scrounge for food, borrow milk or buy on the book (credit arrangements). So I know what it's like to be on the other side of privilege." ; "I worked at an ABC shoe store, Joshua Door, selling furniture, making Irish coffees at Ster Kinekor, waitressing…" ; on treating HIV-positive expectant mothers at Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital in 1993: "In those days, there were no ARVs for children. And so women had to navigate this joy of a new life, with the fact that death was looming over them."

a1388.speaker: Professor Glenda Gray, outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.name: Professor Glenda Gray
a1388.title: outgoing president and chief executive of the SAMRC
a1388.speech: On her reputation for standing up to pressure: "My tongue has gotten me into trouble. How do I feel about that? I just want to make sure that as scientists we let politicians and society know the data and the evidence. I feel passionate about translating science, I feel passionate about evidence. I feel passionate about science changing the world."

a1388.speaker: Dr Zweli Mkhize, then-health minister of South Africa
a1388.name: Dr Zweli Mkhize
a1388.title: then-health minister of South Africa
a1388.speech: Rebuked Gray's claims and sidelined her in the Ministerial Advisory Committee before excluding her from a newly constituted MAC in September.

a1388.speaker: Anban Pillay, acting director-general of health
a1388.name: Anban Pillay
a1388.title: acting director-general of health
a1388.speech: Wrote to the SAMRC board, urging them to investigate Gray's conduct.

a1388.speaker: Guest editorial published in the South African Medical Journal
a1388.name: Guest editorial published in the South African Medical Journal
a1388.speech: Lamented that the council's board was acting in a "sycophantic manner aimed at political appeasement".

a1388.speaker: Clinical trial results (February 2021)
a1388.name: Clinical trial results (February 2021)
a1388.speech: Results from a clinical trial showed that the Oxford AstraZeneca Covid-19 vaccine - then intended for rollout in South Africa - performed poorly in preventing mild to moderate illness caused by the Beta variant of SARS-CoV-2, which was dominant at the time.

a1436.speaker: Vicente Joaquim, Secretary of State for the City of Maputo; Manuel Guilherme Junior, Rector of Eduardo Mondlane University; and Julio Parruque, Mayor of Matola
a1436.name: Vicente Joaquim
a1436.title: Secretary of State for the City of Maputo; Manuel Guilherme Junior, Rector of Eduardo Mondlane University; and Julio Parruque, Mayor of Matola
a1436.speech: describe the journalist Atanasio Marcos, who died last Friday, as a professional of exceptional and high-level qualities. The leaders maintain that Atanasio Marcos's work marked his generation and contributed to the promotion of democracy and the development of the country. The journalist's death is understood as a hard blow, as it was a premature departure. In this moment of pain and dismay, the leaders extend to the bereaved family, to TVM and to the journalistic profession their condolences for the irreparable loss.

a1436.speaker: PRM (Police of the Republic of Mozambique) in the city of Maputo
a1436.name: PRM (Police of the Republic of Mozambique) in the city of Maputo
a1436.speech: confirms the kidnapping of a forty-year-old Lebanese national, which occurred on Saturday morning in the country's capital. The victim is the owner of the Avicena pharmacy and was kidnapped while carrying out business activities by four individuals still at large, armed with firearms.

a1436.speaker: Orio Benzane, new president of Ferroviario de Maputo
a1436.name: Orio Benzane
a1436.title: new president of Ferroviario de Maputo
a1436.speech: has already identified areas that deserve immediate intervention at the club for the institution to function better. Sworn in this Thursday, Benzane says he will work so that Ferroviario becomes a reference in national sport again.

a1436.speaker: Cashew producers of Cuamba district, Niassa province
a1436.name: Cashew producers of Cuamba district
a1436.title: Niassa province
a1436.speech: complain of delays in the provision of chemicals to fight pests in the plantations. According to the producers, the situation could compromise the production expected for this year.

a1436.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1436.name: Daniel Chapo
a1436.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique
a1436.speech: says Mozambique needs a strong private sector and young entrepreneurs with vision in order to achieve Economic Independence.

a1436.speaker: National Association of Young Entrepreneurs (ANJE)
a1436.name: National Association of Young Entrepreneurs (ANJE)
a1436.speech: said it is ready and organised to be part of the solutions, given the country's economic challenges.

a1436.speaker: Commission for Reflection on the Decentralisation Model / participants in the Sofala consultation
a1436.name: Commission for Reflection on the Decentralisation Model / participants in the Sofala consultation
a1436.speech: In the consultation held in Sofala, one of the proposals presented is maintaining the current model but with the elimination of the figure of the administrator in the municipal territory.

a1579.speaker: Norwegian People's Aid (NPA)
a1579.name: Norwegian People's Aid (NPA)
a1579.speech: Despite the ongoing freeze in USAID funding, has pledged to continue supporting South Sudan's media sector and civil society organizations.

a1579.speaker: Henrik Stabell, NPA Country Director (message conveyed by Jacob Atem)
a1579.name: Henrik Stabell
a1579.title: NPA Country Director (message conveyed by Jacob Atem)
a1579.speech: "The message from my BOSS, Henrik Stabell, the NPA Country Director, is that NPA is committed to supporting the media, even though how small it is, NPA will continue supporting a few of you. It may be inadequate, but we'll consistently support you. It may not be much, but we'll always be with you from now until 2029."

a1579.speaker: Jacob Atem, NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.name: Jacob Atem
a1579.title: NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.speech: Acknowledged the difficult circumstances facing media organizations following the USAID funding cut, and assured NPA's unwavering dedication to empowering independent voices in the country: "As NPA, we are still committed to supporting the media and the Civil Society in the country because we know that without the different voices that talk and advocate for the Rights of the people, the Democracy we are talking about cannot be achieved. So, we'll continue supporting you [Media] as NPA."

a1579.speaker: Jacob Atem, NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.name: Jacob Atem
a1579.title: NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.speech: Highlighted the important role NPA plays in the media and in the national media organizations, especially its role in supporting the media with equipment and funds: "As NPA, our role in the media is important, but we are not the ones leading it; we leave it to the national media organizations to play their role." ; "What we do is to support you [media] with the equipment that you need, and with some of the financial resources that you need."

a1579.speaker: Jacob Atem, NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.name: Jacob Atem
a1579.title: NPA's Media Rights Coordinator
a1579.speech: Urged media institutions to think critically outside the box during this very challenging situation to be able to sustain themselves further.

a1594.speaker: Gervais Ndirakobuca, Prime Minister of the Republic of Burundi
a1594.name: Gervais Ndirakobuca
a1594.title: Prime Minister of the Republic of Burundi
a1594.speech: "We discussed the security situation prevailing in eastern DRC in order to find the necessary solutions for the restoration of peace and security," the Burundian head of government indicated ; added that he had shown the heads of state and government of the two Communities that the insecurity prevailing in the DRC disrupts regional security, including that of Burundi, especially with the presence of the terrorist group Red Tabara present in that region ; went on to say that during these meetings measures were taken for the restoration of peace and stability in eastern DRC, citing in particular the immediate cessation of hostilities in order to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of the wounded and the dead.

a1594.speaker: Joint SADC-EAC Summit of heads of state and government
a1594.name: Joint SADC-EAC Summit of heads of state and government
a1594.speech: also concluded that the Rwandan troops supporting the M23 have no reason to be on Congolese soil and must return home, and likewise that the other foreign troops on Congolese soil that were not invited by the Congolese government must leave the country; an unconditional ceasefire, support in humanitarian aid to the victims of the hostilities, the repatriation of the wounded, etc. It was also agreed to establish protection of Goma airport and its surroundings, the roads of the city of Goma, and the opening of the airport and Lake Kivu to facilitate movement; the immediate resumption of dialogue within the framework of the Nairobi process and the Luanda protocol was addressed and the presidents of the two Communities were asked to seek mediators.

a1613.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1613.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.speech: In his speech, encouraged member states to open their borders to promote the sharing of information and technology: "I invite you all to give priority to commercial and regional relations, and to leave the doors of your countries wide open," he affirmed, stressing that this openness will strengthen solidarity and mutual support between nations.

a1613.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1613.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.speech: Addressed a strong message of support to the peoples of the regions affected by insecurity, notably the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Somalia and Sudan: "Solidarity between our nations is paramount to overcoming these challenges," he declared, insisting on the importance of collective action to establish lasting peace in these conflict zones; recalled Burundi's commitment alongside the DRC and other nations in search of peace, affirming that "Burundi allies itself with brother countries within the bilateral and multilateral framework" ; invited member states to a collective awakening to counter foreign armed groups which, according to him, threaten regional integration, adding: "This solidarity will allow the government of the DRC to engage in the inter-Congolese peace process."

a1613.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1613.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.speech: Expressed his confidence in the discussions to come, convinced that this summit will mark "a decisive stage in our common quest for progress and prosperity"; reaffirmed his government's commitment to supporting COMESA's initiatives to strengthen economic ties and build a more resilient and prosperous region.

a1613.speaker: Evariste Ndayishimiye, President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.name: Evariste Ndayishimiye
a1613.title: President of the Republic of Burundi
a1613.speech: Announced: "As of today, Burundi will exempt short-stay visas for all nationals of COMESA member countries."

a1613.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a1613.title: President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.speech: "Member states' exports to the world recorded an increase reaching 219 billion dollars in 2023, compared with 100 billion in 2020. This growth of 210% underlines the importance of regional economic openness," he stressed, adding that in terms of intra-regional trade, trade between COMESA countries has increased by 40%, now reaching 14 billion dollars.

a1613.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a1613.title: President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.speech: Emphasised the ratification of the tripartite free trade area, adopted in July 2024, marking a decisive step towards African integration; this area aims to "establish a unified continental market and improve customs and trade facilitation," he declared, underlining the benefits of a stronger economic union.

a1613.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a1613.title: President of Zambia and outgoing COMESA chair
a1613.speech: In support of small traders, particularly women, affirmed the importance of World Bank-funded projects: "250 million dollars have been allocated to support small traders and women in the Great Lakes region." ; according to Hichilema, the '50 Million African Women Speak' initiative represents a "crucial step towards socially and economically integrating women in our region."

a1675.speaker: Tlohang Sekhamane, Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
a1675.name: Tlohang Sekhamane
a1675.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
a1675.speech: Described youth unemployment as a national emergency that requires urgent and united action from the government and all sectors of society: "Poverty is what Lesotho has been used to for the past 200 years. This country was formed on poverty. But we cannot solve the problem of poverty with the same mind-set that created it."

a1675.speaker: Tlohang Sekhamane, Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
a1675.name: Tlohang Sekhamane
a1675.title: Speaker of the National Assembly of Lesotho
a1675.speech: Criticized the culture of complacency among the youth, saying the youth of this country are in their comfort zone; they do not take action against poor decisions being made today. Basotho cherish poverty, it is time the youth become the solution, as the future of Lesotho depends on them.

a1675.speaker: Kananelo Boloetse, one of the lead organizers of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
a1675.name: Kananelo Boloetse
a1675.title: one of the lead organizers of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
a1675.speech: Announced that young people were working on an Independence Charter, a manifesto that will outline practical steps and policies aimed at achieving economic self-reliance. He stated that this document will serve as a roadmap for the youth and the entire country to move away from dependency on foreign aid and start building their own future.

a1675.speaker: Tumelo Moteuli, organizer of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
a1675.name: Tumelo Moteuli
a1675.title: organizer of the Youth Dialogue on Economic Independence
a1675.speech: Emphasized the importance of learning from the past: "Back in the day, our leaders had strong strategies to unite nations and boost the economy. This dialogue is about reviving those strategies and applying them to today's generation, we need to stop depending on other countries and make sure Lesotho stands on its own feet economically." ; He further explained that the realization that foreign aid is not a sustainable solution was a driving force behind the dialogue, as countries that are poverty-stricken can no longer rely on foreign aid, so they must take charge of their own future.

a1675.speaker: Mohau Mabetha, representing the voices of the youth
a1675.name: Mohau Mabetha
a1675.title: representing the voices of the youth
a1675.speech: Echoed similar sentiments, saying the dialogue serves as an opportunity for young people to brainstorm and develop job creation strategies, stating that the youth need to unite, identify opportunities, and work together to overcome the high unemployment rate, and only then can they improve Lesotho's economy and future.

a1775.speaker: CGTN (news report)
a1775.name: CGTN (news report)
a1775.speech: According to a CGTN news report, the dancing grannies and food delivery drivers on electric scooters got some of the most heartfelt ovations on China's social networks, "Here comes my daily savior!"

a1775.speaker: Tomas Klett, Assistant Professor at the University of St. Gallen
a1775.name: Tomas Klett
a1775.title: Assistant Professor at the University of St. Gallen
a1775.speech: Stated that the United States-China trade dispute might be the initial salvo in this century's first and only Thucydides trap. Theorized by realist thinkers like John Mearsheimer and Graham Allison, that trap sees the incumbent and emerging powers destined for conflict.

a1775.speaker: Tomas Klett, Assistant Professor at the University of St. Gallen
a1775.name: Tomas Klett
a1775.title: Assistant Professor at the University of St. Gallen
a1775.speech: Noted that the West always assumed that a rich China will be "like us." Only five years ago, even many Chinese thought so too. Not anymore, but in a different way than Westerners might expect. As a matter of fact, most Chinese are now disillusioned not with their Communist Party, but with the erratic, leader-less and what many think is the technology-unfriendly, ideology beholden West.

a1775.speaker: Philip Bowring, former editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review and columnist for the International Herald Tribune
a1775.name: Philip Bowring
a1775.title: former editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review and columnist for the International Herald Tribune
a1775.speech: Stressed that there used to be a time when that global narrative was shaped by the United States. Sometimes it was brilliant strategizing like at Bretton Woods, but often that didn't require a lot of activity as the American dream begot voluntary adoration. Those times are gone. It would be a cop-out for the rest of the West, especially Europe, not to check its own act and relevance in the global context.

a1775.speaker: Philip Bowring, former editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review
a1775.name: Philip Bowring
a1775.title: former editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review
a1775.speech: According to Philip Bowring, China does not proselytise; there is deep awareness of the extraordinary performance of its pragmatic domestic development narrative, but China's focus is China. Even the Belt and Road Initiative is an experiment whose story line must yet come into its own; for all the Western nervousness about the BRI today, it is important to realize that BRI does not aim to challenge, but rather seeks to complement the Western narrative. He further noted that part of the reason for the underlying prudence on the Chinese side is awareness that the road to the top is long and setbacks lurk.

a1775.speaker: Robert Shiller, Nobel Prize winner (narrative economics)
a1775.name: Robert Shiller
a1775.title: Nobel Prize winner (narrative economics)
a1775.speech: In Nobel Prize winner Robert Shiller's narrative, the economics discipline analyzes how stories "go viral" and their worldwide "economic impact."

a1775.speaker: Barry Wood, Washington writer and broadcaster
a1775.name: Barry Wood
a1775.title: Washington writer and broadcaster
a1775.speech: Argued that whatever China's drawbacks, which to many Westerners are self-evident, it looks as if it is only China that presently pursues a vision of any kind. The West, meanwhile, either engages in acts of meekness, as Europe does, or seems hell-bent on engaging, as President Donald Trump does, in a prolonged period of dismantling the institutions that bind the world to the Western narrative.

a1775.speaker: Barry Wood, Washington writer and broadcaster
a1775.name: Barry Wood
a1775.title: Washington writer and broadcaster
a1775.speech: According to Barry Wood, the open question is whether the West is ready to renew its global grand narrative for the complex 21st century ahead. That would probably require it to pursue elements that contradict its present positions and which do not emanate from its own traditions.

a1801.speaker: Assitan Coulibaly, youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.name: Assitan Coulibaly
a1801.title: youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.speech: Explained that the quality of the training is one of the reasons she stayed at the Catholic University of West Africa (Ucao): "The quality is there, we have excellent professors" ; specified that she did not initially choose Ucao, because after the baccalaureate she had the choice between France and Canada and was only waiting for a visa, and that her parents enrolled her at Ucao just to pass the time, but when she began the courses she was won over by the quality and the stability of the teaching: "I therefore decided to stay at Ucao in the end and to continue my training."

a1801.speaker: Assitan Coulibaly, youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.name: Assitan Coulibaly
a1801.title: youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.speech: Recalled that from her third bachelor's year she began taking part in competitions, the first being a general legal knowledge contest organised by USAID as part of one of its projects, the "Mali Justice Project", in which her team finished second.

a1801.speaker: Assitan Coulibaly, youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.name: Assitan Coulibaly
a1801.title: youngest candidate admitted to the most recent Malian competitive examination for judicial auditors (aged 21)
a1801.speech: Speaking about the magistracy examination, maintained that she knows plenty of candidates who have no connections, who know no one, who came from their villages and passed the examination; according to her, if they succeeded, that means anyone can succeed too, on condition of working.

a1818.speaker: Illovo Sugar Malawi plc
a1818.name: Illovo Sugar Malawi plc
a1818.speech: Reported that an abnormal surge in domestic sugar demand has severely impacted its export capacity, with overseas sales plummeting to just 6 percent of total production in 2025, down from 46 percent in 2020. The company has attributed the drop to a 53 percent spike in local consumption, raising concerns over smuggling and its effect on Malawi's foreign exchange reserves.

a1818.speaker: Kondwani Msimuko, Interim Managing Director of Illovo Sugar Malawi
a1818.name: Kondwani Msimuko
a1818.title: Interim Managing Director of Illovo Sugar Malawi
a1818.speech: Revealed that Malawi's sugar demand has risen "abnormally, beyond domestic requirements," forcing the company to prioritise local markets ; "We should be asking ourselves: Where is all this sugar going?", hinting at possible smuggling ; "Once we answer that, we can balance local and international markets." ; Cited the demand surge as a primary factor but acknowledged other unspecified challenges contributing to the downturn ; Expressed optimism that exports could rebound if smuggling is managed and production scales up: "We're working to ensure borders are properly managed."

a1818.speaker: Economists and various stakeholders
a1818.name: Economists and various stakeholders
a1818.speech: Have been warning that prolonged export declines could further strain Malawi's fragile economic position, calling for stricter oversight of investments that will focus on production and exports.

a1871.speaker: Ambassador John Nkengasong, US Global AIDS Coordinator
a1871.name: Ambassador John Nkengasong
a1871.title: US Global AIDS Coordinator
a1871.speech: says PEPFAR has invested over N$27 billion in Namibia over the past 18 years ; "PEPFAR is committed in this COPS season to invest over N$1.6 billion. I use that number to assure you that when we discuss sustainability, it is not in the light of us handing over a programme. It is in the spirit of joint responsibility and joint accountability as we move past 2030."

a1871.speaker: Ambassador John Nkengasong, US Global AIDS Coordinator
a1871.name: Ambassador John Nkengasong
a1871.title: US Global AIDS Coordinator
a1871.speech: "Yesterday, at the Katutura State Hospital, I was impressed to see these women who came with us to have a dialogue, and I was honoured to have in my arms one or two of the babies that were HIV-negative, born from HIV-positive mothers who are by themselves very healthy." The smiles they had on their faces told me that they were healthy. They told me that those ladies were carrying the future of your great country in their hands."

a1871.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a1871.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a1871.title: Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a1871.speech: says prior consultation with the affected governments is of the utmost necessity: "These programmes are an integral part of the government's developmental strategy, proper planning and implementation will ensure the continuity of activities. Any reduction in the level of external funding must be done in consultation with the ministry to allow for proper preparation."

a2065.speaker: The New York Times (US newspaper)
a2065.name: The New York Times (US newspaper)
a2065.speech: Reported today, Saturday 1 March 2025, that the United States has formally terminated the contracts through emails and direct letters sent to the institutions coordinating the programmes ; reported that the decision involves important projects such as aid for refugees, tuberculosis (TB) clinics and polio vaccination programmes.

a2065.speaker: US State Department (headed by Marco Rubio)
a2065.name: US State Department (headed by Marco Rubio)
a2065.speech: Sent emails earlier this week terminating funding for refugee camps, TB clinics, polio vaccination projects and thousands of other organisations that depend on US funding for life-saving activities ; stated that these programmes are being terminated in the interests of the US Government.

a2065.speaker: US State Department termination letter (document)
a2065.name: US State Department termination letter (document)
a2065.speech: According to the letter, the cancelled projects include US$131 million in support to Unicef for polio vaccination (planning, supplies and distribution); the 'Chemonics' contract worth US$90 million used against malaria benefiting 53 million people; the FHI 360 project in Yemen for malnourished children; the WHO Global Drug Facility supporting three million TB patients including 300,000 children; the Elizabeth Glaser Foundation HIV programme reaching 350,000 people in Southern Africa; Ebola surveillance in Uganda; US$34 million for medical supplies in Kenya; funding for 87 shelters in South Africa assisting about 33,000 women affected by domestic violence; health services for 3.9 million children and 5.7 million women in Nepal; Helen Keller International's neglected-disease work in West Africa reaching over 35 million people; and malnutrition treatment for 5.6 million children and 1.7 million women in Nigeria.

a2065.speaker: Dr Catherine Kyobutungi, Executive Director of the African Population and Health Research Center
a2065.name: Dr Catherine Kyobutungi
a2065.title: Executive Director of the African Population and Health Research Center
a2065.speech: Said the decision will cause countless deaths, explaining that the exact number may never be known because even the programmes that track deaths have had their funding cut.

a2428.speaker: The Chanzo (investigation by the outlet)
a2428.name: The Chanzo (investigation by the outlet)
a2428.speech: Investigated U.S. dollar availability in Tanzania between September 12 and November 5, 2024, by visiting banks and currency exchange outlets across Dar es Salaam, finding a dollar shortage during the initial survey from September 12 to 14, 2024, with many locations struggling to provide even small sums, and a significant improvement when the same banks and bureaux de change were revisited between October 26 and November 5, with many outlets able to sell sizable amounts for retail purchases ; reported that of the 15 currency exchanges visited in Dar es Salaam, only three were able to provide only $100.

a2428.speaker: Currency exchange operator in Mikocheni, Dar es Salaam (anonymous)
a2428.name: Currency exchange operator in Mikocheni
a2428.title: Dar es Salaam (anonymous)
a2428.speech: “I haven’t seen even $100 in over a week” ; “We only have Euros at the moment.” Later, in the November visit, he was ready to offer over 1,000: “Bring a printed travel document or other supporting document, and you’ll get them.”

a2428.speaker: Currency operator in Msasani, Dar es Salaam (anonymous)
a2428.name: Currency operator in Msasani
a2428.title: Dar es Salaam (anonymous)
a2428.speech: “You can get $100, but you’ll have to come back later.”

a2428.speaker: Currency exchange operator (anonymous, visibly frustrated)
a2428.name: Currency exchange operator (anonymous
a2428.title: visibly frustrated)
a2428.speech: Explained why U.S. dollars were scarce: “Customers don’t bring dollars here; they’re selling them in the streets at inflated rates.”

a2428.speaker: Official from one of Tanzania’s top banks (anonymous)
a2428.name: Official from one of Tanzania’s top banks (anonymous)
a2428.speech: “Each branch is rationed about $1,000 daily for walk-in customers.”

a2428.speaker: Bank customer seeking $150 for a visa application (anonymous)
a2428.name: Bank customer seeking $150 for a visa application (anonymous)
a2428.speech: Expressed frustration to the reporter while waiting to confirm dollar availability: “I was directed to this branch, but now I don’t know what’s going on.”

a2428.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a2428.name: Government of Tanzania
a2428.speech: In May 2023, officially acknowledged the dollar shortage, attributing it largely to a current account deficit that reached $5.4 billion in 2022.

a2428.speaker: Dr Mouhsin Masoud, former university lecturer and banker
a2428.name: Dr Mouhsin Masoud
a2428.title: former university lecturer and banker
a2428.speech: Explained the trend of rising dollar deposits at the 21st Conference of Financial Institutions in March 2024, saying, “In the bank, you can have a lot of dollars in customers’ accounts, but they’re not available for sale.”

a2428.speaker: Bank of Tanzania (BoT), July 2024 Monetary Policy Statement
a2428.name: Bank of Tanzania (BoT)
a2428.title: July 2024 Monetary Policy Statement
a2428.speech: “Banks’ foreign currency deposits maintained an upward trend since January 2024, driven by high returns favoring holding and transacting in foreign currency.”

a2428.speaker: Elias Lukumay, Chairperson of the Tanzania Truck Owners Association
a2428.name: Elias Lukumay
a2428.title: Chairperson of the Tanzania Truck Owners Association
a2428.speech: Explained on February 28, 2024, during the national tax forum: “On the issue of the dollar, the Government has put a cap, no Bank will change above the rate of 2500 or 2550 but in the street, dollars are there, because they are exchanged at 2700 to 2800. Dollars are not staying in Banks because the rate is lower than the streets.”

a2428.speaker: Raphael Mgaya, Executive Director of the Tanzania Association of Oil Marketing Companies (TAOMAC)
a2428.name: Raphael Mgaya
a2428.title: Executive Director of the Tanzania Association of Oil Marketing Companies (TAOMAC)
a2428.speech: Highlighted a notable improvement in the market: “The situation has improved, it’s not like the way it used to be, but we are not there yet.” ; explained that there are still some instances where they have to use Euros in place of dollars.

a2428.speaker: Trader in Kariakoo who imports beauty items from China (anonymous)
a2428.name: Trader in Kariakoo who imports beauty items from China (anonymous)
a2428.speech: “We have local banks that you can deposit shillings and you get Yuan while in China” ; shared that the only issue is that to get the Yuan, the Tsh currency is first calculated in USD and then exchanged again to Yuan, causing a double loss in the exchange rate.

a2428.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) report
a2428.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) report
a2428.speech: “If left unaddressed, re-emerging pressures in the foreign exchange market could undermine Tanzania’s hard-earned macro-financial stability. The BoT should encourage banks and bureau de changes to trade at market clearing exchange rates, and conduct foreign exchange interventions in accordance with the new policy while maintaining adequate foreign exchange reserves” ; through its recovery programme, required Tanzania to reduce central bank intervention in the market and allow banks and bureaux de change to use the market rate.

a2503.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.name: Bill Gates
a2503.title: Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.speech: "The picture of the world's richest man killing the world's poorest children is not a pretty one," Gates told the Financial Times on Thursday, in a stinging rebuke directed at Musk ; said the sweeping aid reductions, implemented by Musk's department, have "decimated" USAID's ability to support life-saving initiatives, including vaccinations for children and emergency food assistance for vulnerable populations.

a2503.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist (statement published on his website)
a2503.name: Bill Gates
a2503.title: Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist (statement published on his website)
a2503.speech: "People will say a lot of things about me when I die, but I am determined that 'he died rich' will not be one of them. There are too many urgent problems to solve for me to hold onto resources that could be used to help people."

a2503.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.name: Bill Gates
a2503.title: Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.speech: "It's unclear whether the world's richest countries will continue to stand up for its poorest people," he said, pointing to reduced commitments from the United States, the United Kingdom and France; he warned that without government support, even the foundation's substantial resources would not be enough to sustain progress in global health, and stated that using polio as an example, eradication efforts would likely fail without U.S. funding: "Polio would not be eradicated."

a2503.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.name: Bill Gates
a2503.title: Microsoft co-founder and philanthropist
a2503.speech: Maintained that billionaires have a responsibility to act: "I hope other wealthy people consider how much they can accelerate progress for the world's poorest if they increased the pace and scale of their giving, because it is such a profoundly impactful way to give back to society."

a2560.speaker: Yousef Al-Tunayan, Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a2560.name: Yousef Al-Tunayan
a2560.title: Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a2560.speech: Said member states must demonstrate their willingness to act on the principles upon which the bloc was founded ; “Somalia’s situation represents a real test of whether we can transform words into action,” underscoring Kuwait’s support for Somalia’s sovereignty, political independence, and territorial integrity.

a2560.speaker: Yousef Al-Tunayan, Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.name: Yousef Al-Tunayan
a2560.title: Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.speech: Welcomed recent milestones by the Somali government, including its election to a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for 2025–2026, and praised Somalia’s ongoing efforts to strengthen public institutions, improve security, and establish the rule of law—despite ongoing economic and climate-related challenges.

a2560.speaker: Yousef Al-Tunayan, Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.name: Yousef Al-Tunayan
a2560.title: Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.speech: Commended the World Bank’s decision to grant debt relief to Somalia, describing it as a key step toward economic stability and development; said the relief could help expand basic services and create new growth opportunities.

a2560.speaker: Yousef Al-Tunayan, Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.name: Yousef Al-Tunayan
a2560.title: Kuwait's Permanent Representative to the OIC
a2560.speech: Noted that Kuwait has continued to provide humanitarian and development assistance to Somalia through official government channels and charitable organizations, focused on essential sectors such as education, health, clean water, food security, and youth empowerment ; concluded by emphasizing that sustainable development is the foundation of lasting peace and reiterated Kuwait’s commitment to partnering with Somalia on its path to recovery.

a2681.speaker: Kyeh Kim, senior MCC official
a2681.name: Kyeh Kim
a2681.title: senior MCC official
a2681.speech: “Foreign aid is not a priority for the administration and so MCC’s work needs to wind down,” Kyeh Kim, a senior MCC official, told staff. Said officials from DOGE arrived at the agency early last week and entered talks with leadership, who were attempting to save the agency.

a2681.speaker: Kyeh Kim, senior MCC official (advice to staff)
a2681.name: Kyeh Kim
a2681.title: senior MCC official (advice to staff)
a2681.speech: “I would encourage you to think very hard of what makes sense for you and your family at this time, and that is more important than your commitment to this organization,” Kim said in the meeting on Wednesday, warning that the organization’s future “looks very stark.”

a2681.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2681.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2681.speech: The MCC did not respond to an email requesting comment.

a2681.speaker: President Donald Trump and adviser Elon Musk
a2681.name: President Donald Trump and adviser Elon Musk
a2681.speech: Saying U.S. taxpayer money is misspent, in an unprecedented push to shrink the federal government.

a2681.speaker: MCC employee (anonymous)
a2681.name: MCC employee (anonymous)
a2681.speech: Told Reuters all the agency’s work had been ordered halted apart from a small number of active construction projects, including a wastewater treatment plant in Mongolia, electrical power grids in Senegal and Nepal, and schools in Ivory Coast. “This is very much a business- and infrastructure-focused way of doing development. It’s very much in America’s interest,” said the employee, who requested anonymity.

a2681.speaker: MCC recording of staff meeting
a2681.name: MCC recording of staff meeting
a2681.speech: MCC staff were told in a meeting on Wednesday that all of the agency’s programs will be closed and staff numbers would be minimized, according to a recording of the meeting.

a2681.speaker: Politico
a2681.name: Politico
a2681.speech: First reported the move, citing an email sent to staff at the agency on Tuesday, which Reuters has also reviewed.

a2681.speaker: Email to MCC staff
a2681.name: Email to MCC staff
a2681.speech: Gives the agency’s 300 or so staff until April 29 to decide whether to take voluntary early retirement or a deferred resignation under which they will receive pay until the end of September, or face being placed on administrative leave.

a2681.speaker: MCC website
a2681.name: MCC website
a2681.speech: It partners with developing countries on projects like improving electricity supply for businesses and improving roads for farmers to get their goods to market, according to its website.

a2761.speaker: International Crisis Group (ICG)
a2761.name: International Crisis Group (ICG)
a2761.speech: Suggested that African heads of state convening in Ethiopia should look into eight key areas: "The AU should focus on in 2023: Reforming its institutions; nurturing agreements in Ethiopia and Sudan; urging regional cooperation around the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam; easing tensions in the Great Lakes and Central Africa; and steering talks to unlock Libya's stalemated transition."

a2761.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (statement)
a2761.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2761.title: President of South Africa (statement)
a2761.speech: Said the AfCFTA would be a top priority for the southern African region at the AU Summit: "South Africa, together with our neighbours in the Southern African Customs Union, will soon finalise our industrial offer on the African Continental Free Trade Area. Once fully operationalised, the Continental Free Trade will provide an unprecedented opportunity to deepen African economic integration, grow national economies, and open up new frontiers and markets for South African companies."

a2761.speaker: Media reports in Algeria
a2761.name: Media reports in Algeria
