a2761.speech: Claim that the recent visit to South Africa by Algerian foreign minister Ramtane Lamamra was part of a plan to lobby for South Africa's support on stripping Israel's observer status at the AU.

a2761.speaker: US delegation / Office of the spokesperson (statement)
a2761.name: US delegation / Office of the spokesperson (statement)
a2761.speech: The US delegation said it would meet with stakeholders to discuss the global food security crisis, and its disproportionate impact on Africa, as well as to follow up on US commitments made at the US-Africa Leaders Summit: "The US delegation will reinforce US commitment to advance food security and highlight the ongoing work through the US government's Feed the Future initiative, and efforts to scale up work on climate-resilient agriculture and soil health, including upcoming work on the Vision for Adapted Crops and Soils (VACS)."

a2774.speaker: Core Public Servants (CPS), congratulatory letter signed by Kudirat Akindero
a2774.name: Core Public Servants (CPS)
a2774.title: congratulatory letter signed by Kudirat Akindero
a2774.speech: Hailed President Bola Tinubu for appointing Dr Adebowale Adedokun as Director General of the Bureau of Public Procurement, lauding the President for following due process and picking the most qualified to run the affairs of the specialised agency: "Congratulations to Dr. Adebowale Adedokun, PhD (MCIPS, CMILT), on his appointment as the Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP)." ; "This significant achievement reflects his extensive expertise and unwavering dedication to advancing public procurement in Nigeria." ; "With over 20 years of robust experience in public service, Dr. Adedokun has made substantial contributions to procurement reform." ; "His distinguished academic background includes a doctorate in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, complemented by four master's degrees in Procurement, Finance, Technology, and Transportation Management." ; "This diverse educational foundation equips him with a comprehensive understanding of the complexities inherent in procurement processes." ; "In his career, Dr. Adedokun has held pivotal roles, including serving as a National Consultant for the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on public procurement reforms." ; "He represents Nigeria in the International Research Study on Public Procurement (IRSPP) and serves as a World Bank Resource Person on Sustainable Procurement. His commitment to capacity building is evident in his training of over 4,000 federal and state government procurement professionals nationwide." ; "Additionally, he has been instrumental as the focal point officer for the UN Women Project aimed at empowering women in procurement in Nigeria and as the Project Coordinator/Procurement Node for the SPESSE - World Bank Project." ; "His leadership is expected to advance efficiency, transparency, and accountability within Nigeria's public procurement system."

a2846.speaker: Family members of the two deceased (Kiiungoni Village, South Pemba)
a2846.name: Family members of the two deceased (Kiiungoni Village
a2846.title: South Pemba)
a2846.speech: Claimed they were put under pressure to bury the bodies quickly, and that it was soldiers of the National Service (JKU) who transported the bodies and dug the graves, something that appeared unusual.

a2846.speaker: Othman Masoud Othman, First Vice-President of Zanzibar
a2846.name: Othman Masoud Othman
a2846.title: First Vice-President of Zanzibar
a2846.speech: Explained that when he went to Pemba, where the deaths of Othman Hamad Othman (75) and Amour Salim Khamis (28) occurred, the legal procedure (inquest) did not appear to have been properly carried out ; called, when opening the North Pemba Regional Court building at Kinyasini, Wete District, for a legal inquest to be conducted so that the truth of the matter be known and justice be seen to be done ; asked the Court, the Police and the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions to ensure that a legal inquest is conducted into such suspicious deaths.

a2846.speaker: Abdullah Musa, Senior Assistant Commissioner, Regional Police Commander of South Pemba
a2846.name: Abdullah Musa
a2846.title: Senior Assistant Commissioner, Regional Police Commander of South Pemba
a2846.speech: Says they will investigate the matter and give an explanation.

a2846.speaker: Police (Zanzibar Police Force)
a2846.name: Police (Zanzibar Police Force)
a2846.speech: Have admitted arresting the two men on allegations of involvement in the drug trade ; say they are investigating.

a2846.speaker: Professor Omar Faki, Representative for Pandani, Pemba, and family members of the deceased
a2846.name: Professor Omar Faki
a2846.title: Representative for Pandani, Pemba, and family members of the deceased
a2846.speech: Have accused the state security organs of involvement in the killings ; say both bodies showed that the men had been beaten, and that photographs that were circulated show injuries on the bodies.

a2846.speaker: Omar Fakih, sheha (local government leader) of the area
a2846.name: Omar Fakih
a2846.title: sheha (local government leader) of the area
a2846.speech: Claims he saw the bodies of the deceased and that they were clean, without even a scratch.

a2846.speaker: Some politicians (unnamed)
a2846.name: Some politicians (unnamed)
a2846.speech: Demanded that the Police should not be questioned about such suspicious deaths, on the claim that to do so is to interfere with the work of the Police Force.

a2847.speaker: Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC)
a2847.name: Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC)
a2847.speech: Announced on Monday the completion of trials for 264 freight wagons designed for its electric train operating on the new Standard Gauge Railway (SGR).

a2847.speaker: Felchesmi Mramba, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Energy
a2847.name: Felchesmi Mramba
a2847.title: Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Energy
a2847.speech: Has clarified that Tanzania’s decision to purchase electricity from Ethiopia through Kenya to Namanga, Arusha, will enhance power supply in the northern regions ; stated that the primary goal of buying or selling electricity is to strengthen national power grids and reduce costs, and explained that the northern regions currently rely heavily on electricity generated in the southern regions ; "These agreements are two-way. At times, we will buy electricity, and at other times, we will use the same route to sell power to neighboring countries. For now, considering the energy situation in the north, we will be purchasing more than we supply. However, there will be times when they may need electricity, and we will use the same route to deliver it to them."

a2847.speaker: Ministry of Health of the United Republic of Tanzania (statement)
a2847.name: Ministry of Health of the United Republic of Tanzania (statement)
a2847.speech: Has announced the confirmation of two cases of the virus that causes Mpox, the first time the disease has been detected in the country ; according to the Ministry’s statement, one of the suspects was a truck driver who had traveled from a neighboring country and entered Dar es Salaam ; stated that in collaboration with the President’s Office (RALG) and all healthcare facilities, it continues to monitor, investigate, and identify any additional suspected cases to ensure timely medical intervention.

a2847.speaker: Unnamed individual in a video circulated online
a2847.name: Unnamed individual in a video circulated online
a2847.speech: "Hey, Brother Masoud, I’ve been given a bed here. They call this place Kipawa, Kipawa Majani ya Chai. There’s a VETA school, and right there at VETA, there’s a hospital where I have been admitted. I’ve been brought here with other patients with this disease. We are all here, receiving treatment. Even if you come to see me, you won’t be allowed to enter. You will stand outside, and maybe I will step out, but we will talk through the window."

a2847.speaker: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) army
a2847.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) army
a2847.speech: Reported on Monday the arrest of two individuals who identified themselves as Tanzanians, suspected of being recruited by the ISIS-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).

a2847.speaker: U.S. Department of State
a2847.name: U.S. Department of State
a2847.speech: According to the U.S. Department of State, the group established ties with ISIS in 2018.

a2847.speaker: Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM) official party statement
a2847.name: Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM) official party statement
a2847.speech: Indicated that, in addition to other discussions, the NEC meeting also conducted the selection of candidates for various leadership positions within CCM and its affiliated organizations that were previously vacant.

a2847.speaker: CCM announcement of the meeting (released March 8, 2025)
a2847.name: CCM announcement of the meeting (released March 8
a2847.speech: Stated that the NEC meeting would be preceded by a Central Committee meeting, which is also chaired by the party’s national chairperson.

a2932.speaker: Francisco Pereira, PAICV deputy (Cape Verde National Assembly)
a2932.name: Francisco Pereira
a2932.title: PAICV deputy (Cape Verde National Assembly)
a2932.speech: “External relations are based on credibility and on coherence of positions. Regrettably this has not been the hallmark of the MpD Government, led by Prime Minister Ulisses Correia e Silva. This Government’s foreign policy is adrift” ; said that since independence Cape Verde has consolidated a diplomatic posture based on mutual respect, non-interference in internal affairs and strict respect for International Law, which allowed the country to assert itself internationally in organisations such as the UN, ECOWAS and the CPLP ; “We have been witnessing a diplomacy devoid of strategic vision and patriotic sense. In recent times, a clear break with the pragmatic principles of our external action can be noted” ; “Who does not remember the diplomatic catastrophe with the appointment of the honorary consul in Florida? The country faced an unprecedented and complex situation,” referring to a foreign policy that he considers “was contaminated by far-right ideological sectors”.

a2932.speaker: PAICV (party position in the debate)
a2932.name: PAICV (party position in the debate)
a2932.speech: Pointed to the handling of the visa exemption process for citizens of the European Union and the United Kingdom, parliamentary approval of the SOFA agreement, and the candidacy for the presidency of ECOWAS; also criticised the recognition of the territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Morocco, which it considers a disregard for United Nations guidelines, and Cape Verde’s abstention on a UN resolution on the humanitarian corridor in the Gaza Strip.

a2932.speaker: Aniceto Barbosa, vice-president of the leadership of the MpD parliamentary group
a2932.name: Aniceto Barbosa
a2932.title: vice-president of the leadership of the MpD parliamentary group
a2932.speech: Highlighted that, for the country, establishing innovative partnerships is essential, and emphasised the central role of multisectoral diplomacy aligned with constitutional principles: “Partnerships that attract investment, drive the internationalisation of companies, strengthen our diaspora and promote our cultural identity beyond our borders” ; considered that Cape Verdean diplomacy has been recognised worldwide for the political, institutional and social stability of the country, as well as for advances in freedom, democracy and transparency: “Cape Verde’s ‘soft power’ has stood out in international rankings. We are the freest African country in the index of civil and political liberties, the third in the democracy index, and the second in the index of economic freedom and of transparency and corruption” ; mentioned among recent advances Cape Verde’s selection for a new Millennium Challenge Corporation compact and the financial support of 319 million euros from the European Union through the Global Gateway programme, and the strengthening of bilateral and multilateral relations ; “Our diplomacy is at the service of Cape Verde, of Africa and of the World. We have contributed to building a fairer international order and mitigated the impact of global crises.”

a3054.speaker: Ministry of Trade of Malawi
a3054.name: Ministry of Trade of Malawi
a3054.speech: has said Malawi is expected to commence trading under the Guided Trade Initiative (GTI) of the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) within the next three months.

a3054.speaker: Patrick Botha, Ministry of Trade spokesperson
a3054.name: Patrick Botha
a3054.title: Ministry of Trade spokesperson
a3054.speech: In a written response to a questionnaire, described the upcoming trade as a milestone that would provide a practical framework for testing trade mechanisms, resolving challenges boosting intra-African trade. "Although Malawi has not yet started trading under the GTI, several critical preparatory activities have been completed, and some companies have already expressed interest in participating" ; said the ministry had launched various initiatives to enhance private sector participation in AfCFTA, including training on trade protocols, implementation modalities and available market opportunities ; said operational tools such as the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), which allows companies to trade in local currencies, were ready for deployment, adding that Malawian banks had adopted the system and were preparing to go live ; lauded the Malawi Revenue Authority's recent launch of the online E-Tariff Book, which has digitised all Harmonised System (HS) codes across all trade agreements, including the AfCFTA.

a3054.speaker: The Economic Report on Africa 2025 by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca)
a3054.name: The Economic Report on Africa 2025 by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (Uneca)
a3054.speech: underscored the AfCFTA's potential in addressing the continent's socio-economic challenges. The report calls for accelerated implementation of the agreement, reducing tariffs, eliminating non-tariff barriers, harmonising trade policies across member states, developing regional value chains and integrating climate policies into AfCFTA implementation strategies.

a3054.speaker: Bridgepath Capital Limited (financial institution), in its review of the Uneca report
a3054.name: Bridgepath Capital Limited (financial institution)
a3054.title: in its review of the Uneca report
a3054.speech: stressed the binding nature of the AfCFTA agreement, urging State parties to conduct a comprehensive review of domestic policies and laws, address any gaps and ensure alignment with AfCFTA standards.

a3054.speaker: Edward Chilima, economist
a3054.name: Edward Chilima
a3054.title: economist
a3054.speech: said participation in the AfCFTA would open Malawi to a much larger market for its goods and services.

a3211.speaker: Pro-choice activists
a3211.name: Pro-choice activists
a3211.speech: Say neither restrictive laws nor religious sermons have deterred women from seeking clandestine abortions that reportedly kill up to 18 in every 100 pregnant women nationwide.

a3211.speaker: Emma Kaliya, Coalition for Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (Copua) chairperson
a3211.name: Emma Kaliya
a3211.title: Coalition for Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (Copua) chairperson
a3211.speech: “With or without Trump’s order, the movement in Malawi will neither die nor slow down.” ; “I know that those opposed to the movement will use Trump’s order to their advantage, but we can do our advocacy with or without Trump so long it serves our people well.”

a3211.speaker: Hastings Saka, Malawi Sexual Reproductive Health Rights Alliance national coordinator
a3211.name: Hastings Saka
a3211.title: Malawi Sexual Reproductive Health Rights Alliance national coordinator
a3211.speech: Says the country may be hit hard “unless the global north steps in to close the gap” created by the closure of US aid taps ; “Malawi will indeed be affected by reductions in resources going to government and partners.”

a3211.speaker: Godfrey Kangaunde, Nyale Institute executive director
a3211.name: Godfrey Kangaunde
a3211.title: Nyale Institute executive director
a3211.speech: “The funds partner organisations had been receiving through USAid have already dried up and will likely continue to diminish, limiting the resources available for advancing the safe abortion campaign in the country.” ; urges pro-choice organisations to engage an extra gear to find sustainable funding in the wake of the global gag.

a3211.speaker: Michael Kaiyatsa, Malawi Human Rights and Rehabilitation executive director
a3211.name: Michael Kaiyatsa
a3211.title: Malawi Human Rights and Rehabilitation executive director
a3211.speech: Says restricting non-governmental organisations’ ability to provide abortion services and information creates “a chilling effect on SRH advocacy and support”.

a3211.speaker: Michael Kaiyatsa, Malawi Human Rights and Rehabilitation executive director
a3211.name: Michael Kaiyatsa
a3211.title: Malawi Human Rights and Rehabilitation executive director
a3211.speech: During the meeting in Lilongwe: “Instead of focussing on Trump’s negative energy, we should draw inspiration from the resilience shown by [pro-choice] advocates globally.” ; “The gag rule reminds us of the urgent need to amplify our voices and stand firm in our commitment to reproductive health justice.”

a3211.speaker: Rebecca Hart Holder, Reproductive Equity Now president
a3211.name: Rebecca Hart Holder
a3211.title: Reproductive Equity Now president
a3211.speech: Told The Guardian that Trump’s order may result in more women losing lives to pregnancy complications.

a3211.speaker: Emma Kaliya, Coalition for Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (Copua) chairperson
a3211.name: Emma Kaliya
a3211.title: Coalition for Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (Copua) chairperson
a3211.speech: Says the US conference is likely to discuss the Global Gag Rule “if it’s a common concern” ; “At that meeting, you negotiate as a bloc and Malawi aligns with the African Union. What is sad is that Trump’s order affects women the most.”

a3211.speaker: Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a3211.name: Ministry of Health (Malawi)
a3211.speech: Reports that unsafe abortion accounts for 18 percent of maternal deaths nationwide, with 60 percent of the survivors seeking medical treatment for costly complications.

a3211.speaker: Health workers
a3211.name: Health workers
a3211.speech: Say many patients arrive in critical conditions.

a3237.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a3237.title: President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.speech: Called for a genuine scientific, technological and industrial revolution and urged Burkinabe citizens to break with external dependence and build the foundations of lasting sovereignty themselves ; praised the commitment of Burkinabe researchers and innovators and announced the equipping of the country with latest-generation research equipment by the first quarter of 2026, to be installed in a technology centre giving every inventor the tools to realise his ideas ; insisted that from now on companies will be required to contribute to research and innovation, in a logic of collective self-sufficiency ; announced a fivefold increase in the rewards intended for inventors.

a3237.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a3237.title: President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.speech: Bluntly denounced the intellectual laziness and consumerism that hold back the continent's development: "If Africa is the cradle of humanity, one has to ask why it is last today" ; said many citizens use only a tiny part of their capacities and hide behind imported models of work unsuited to today's demands, and called for a collective surge founded on work, rigour and creativity.

a3237.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a3237.title: President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.speech: Railed against excessive imports that drain the country's coffers for basic products such as clothing, fans, air conditioners or office furniture, and ruled that from now on no luxury furniture will be imported for the administration, the State giving priority to local production and encouraging Burkinabe artisans, carpenters and welders to meet national needs.

a3237.speaker: Captain Ibrahim Traore, President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.name: Captain Ibrahim Traore
a3237.title: President of Faso, Head of State of Burkina Faso
a3237.speech: Underlined the importance of innovation in national defence in the context of the war against terrorism and invited scientists to become involved in the local production of engines, powder and explosives to strengthen the country's operational capacity ; promised direct support from the Presidency and reaffirmed that Burkina Faso needs researchers who are both competent and patriotic: "Having a head full of knowledge is not enough, you must also have a heart full of patriotism."

a3319.speaker: Petra Pereyra, EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.name: Petra Pereyra
a3319.title: EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.speech: Told the media this week that EU has been teaming up with the government of Botswana on two main priorities - to bring transformation and economic diversification, as well as job creation ; said diversification of the economy and job creation, especially for the youth, will be crucial for further development of Botswana to increase the resilience of the economy to external shocks.

a3319.speaker: Petra Pereyra, EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.name: Petra Pereyra
a3319.title: EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.speech: On lessons that the African Union (AU) can take from the established EU trade bloc, said there are several takeaways: the EU is very diverse but united in diversity; “European integration and single market, the largest in the world did not happen overnight and it is a very long process,” she said, further stating that the process started in the early 1950s after the second World War; another lesson is that in the first 10 years, between 300 000 and 900 000 jobs were created thanks to the single market ; said for smaller markets like Botswana, it is great to have an opportunity to trade within a larger market like SADC and the AfCFTA ; “That is why the Agreement is worth preserving. We appreciate the work we continue to do together with the SADC Secretariat to facilitate trade links within the SADC region. We also appreciate the fact that Botswana has joined the AfCFTA and hope to see the successful implementation of the trade Agreement.”

a3319.speaker: Petra Pereyra, EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.name: Petra Pereyra
a3319.title: EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.speech: Said the EU has supported the AfCFTA with over EURO 74 million earlier before 2020 through the Pan-African programme, funding which has been helping with capacity building, negotiation and ratification programme of the trade agreement, as well as supporting African governments in putting the agreement into motion ; “We have an initiative with member states in supporting the implementation of the Agreement.”

a3319.speaker: Petra Pereyra, EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.name: Petra Pereyra
a3319.title: EU Ambassador to Botswana and SADC
a3319.speech: Said they have not yet determined the length of the partnership in hosting the Global Expo in partnership with the Ministry of Trade and Industry through the BITC ; “We will have to take stock of the event afterwards to see what fruit it bears and what we can do better in the future and how we can do this in a way that it is productive and impactful as possible.”

a3319.speaker: Ellen Richard-Madisa, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Trade
a3319.name: Ellen Richard-Madisa
a3319.title: Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Trade
a3319.speech: Explained that on an annual basis depending on a theme that is being promoted, different partners may be engaged to ensure that the theme is articulated well ; “Last year we partnered with Afrixem Bank and we know that that partnership has resulted in better things. We have further partnered with them in assisting businesses in Botswana with capacity building and funding” ; added that Botswana has always partnered with the EU and the belief is that this particular partnership regarding the Global Expo is the beginning of another aspect of the relationship that will see more EU investors coming to participate in the Global Expo in the coming years.

a3435.speaker: Sultan Mohammed Al Shamsi, UAE Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs for Development Affairs and International Organisations and member of the International Humanitarian and Philanthropic Council
a3435.name: Sultan Mohammed Al Shamsi
a3435.title: UAE Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs for Development Affairs and International Organisations and member of the International Humanitarian and Philanthropic Council
a3435.speech: Affirmed the continued support of the United Arab Emirates, its leadership, its government and its people for the Lebanese people, to assist recovery, achieve security and stability, and provide basic materials such as medicines and medical supplies, given the current difficult conditions ; stressed that, under the directives of the Emirati leadership, the UAE is a global leader in supporting people affected by wars, conflicts, disasters and crises ; noted that the UAE will continue its relief efforts for the Lebanese people, both in Lebanon and among Lebanese refugees in Syria, providing essential supplies and basic needs to everyone.

a3524.speaker: Delegation from Malawi College of Health Sciences
a3524.name: Delegation from Malawi College of Health Sciences
a3524.speech: Informed the Education, Science and Technology Cluster Committee of Parliament on Tuesday that insufficient disbursement of funds from the 2024/25 National Budget, combined with the withdrawal of the United States Agency for International Development (USAid) support, has resulted in a funding gap that endangers the institution’s capacity for growth.

a3524.speaker: Alice Kadango, executive director of Malawi College of Health Sciences
a3524.name: Alice Kadango
a3524.title: executive director of Malawi College of Health Sciences
a3524.speech: Said they need resources to recruit specialist lecturers, maintain the institution’s infrastructure and acquire a new fleet of vehicles to replace the ageing ones ; “No funds have been allocated to complete the construction of classrooms and laboratories” ; said the institution would require approximately K3.5 billion to acquire a new fleet of vehicles and recruit specialist lecturers for its degree programmes.

a3524.speaker: Malawi College of Health Sciences presentation to Parliament (document)
a3524.name: Malawi College of Health Sciences presentation to Parliament (document)
a3524.speech: According to a copy of the presentation The Nation obtained, the college was allocated K500 million in the 2024/25 National Budget; however, none of these funds was disbursed as of January, and the institution received K1.68 billion in government subventions from an allocated K2.2 billion.

a3524.speaker: Treasury officials
a3524.name: Treasury officials
a3524.speech: Indicated at the meeting that the department had approved the disbursement of K100 million, which is yet to be remitted to the college, and that the other K400 million was trimmed during the Mid-Year Budget Review Meeting.

a3524.speaker: Brainax Kaise, chairperson of the Education, Science and Technology Cluster Committee
a3524.name: Brainax Kaise
a3524.title: chairperson of the Education, Science and Technology Cluster Committee
a3524.speech: Pledged to lobby the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs as well as the Ministry of Education, to explore budgetary manoeuvres that would facilitate the institution’s growth.

a3686.speaker: Yves Kafando, Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.name: Yves Kafando
a3686.title: Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.speech: Stressed that this meeting is part of the drive to refocus the missions assigned to the customs administration, thus heralding promising prospects for all stakeholders ; “Together, we have the historic duty to consolidate a framework of collaboration founded on transparency, mutual trust and a thorough understanding of the special customs regimes from which you benefit. This dialogue is an essential lever for strengthening our partnership and guaranteeing a harmonious and effective application of our reciprocal commitments.”

a3686.speaker: Yves Kafando, Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.name: Yves Kafando
a3686.title: Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.speech: Recalled the central role of his institution within the Ministry of Finance: “It ensures not only the implementation of customs and tax legislation, but also the rigorous monitoring of the exemptions granted to NGOs and associations” ; explained that NGOs and associations enjoy a certain number of tax and customs privileges linked to the importation of goods and services indispensable to carrying out their missions ; “These measures are intended to encourage and support your actions in the service of Burkina Faso’s development. Our main challenge, as an administration, is to ensure an equitable, transparent and uniform management of these specific regimes, in order to optimise your performance and guarantee a quality service.”

a3686.speaker: Yves Kafando, Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.name: Yves Kafando
a3686.title: Divisional Customs Inspector and Director General of Customs of Burkina Faso
a3686.speech: Announced that, as part of the implementation of its 2022-2026 strategic plan, his institution has initiated several actions intended to strengthen communication and collaboration with its partners ; indicated that this meeting would serve as a platform for revising the legal bases relating to customs franchises, exemptions and applicable taxation, with a view to better ownership by all stakeholders ; affirmed that this meeting marks the starting point of a dynamic synergy and of continuous consultation between the various actors.

a3686.speaker: Alimatou Zongo, née Kaboré, Director of Partnership with NGOs, Development Associations and Foundations
a3686.name: Alimatou Zongo
a3686.title: née Kaboré, Director of Partnership with NGOs, Development Associations and Foundations
a3686.speech: Said this interaction will enable the actors to fully grasp the regulations so as to operate with greater effectiveness: “These rules, although provided for by the texts and laws in force, are often unknown or misinterpreted by the diversity of actors. Yet they constitute an important lever for strengthening the effectiveness and impact of the activities carried out in the field by NGOs, development associations and foundations.”

a3724.speaker: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh, United Nations Resident Coordinator
a3724.name: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh
a3724.title: United Nations Resident Coordinator
a3724.speech: Urged Malawi to look inward and develop its own solutions to drive growth and support the implementation of its national development agenda; says the global development cooperation landscape is becoming increasingly challenging, and countries like Malawi must strengthen domestic resource mobilisation efforts to sustain progress ; “When you have friends who support you, it is a good thing. But when the time comes that they can no longer support you, then you have to look internally. That is where the UN is stepping in; to support Malawi in building the capacity to mobilise its own resources. It is a long road, but it is doable.”

a3724.speaker: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh, United Nations Resident Coordinator
a3724.name: Rebecca Adda-Dontoh
a3724.title: United Nations Resident Coordinator
a3724.speech: Commended the media for its role in promoting development goals and supporting the general elections scheduled for September 16; called for peace, tolerance and inclusivity among citizens, political parties and candidates; underlined the media’s crucial responsibility as the fourth estate in fostering meaningful dialogue and advocating for a peaceful electoral process ; “For us, independent media is very critical in accelerating the achievement of Malawi 2063 and the Sustainable Development Goals. We came here to appreciate the work of the media and of The Times Group in particular, and to challenge you to continue supporting Malawi’s development journey.”

a3724.speaker: Country Focus Report, African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3724.name: Country Focus Report
a3724.title: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a3724.speech: Projected that Malawi faces a financing gap of $3.59 billion to fast-track its structural transformation by 2030; according to the AfDB, the country requires $4.5 billion through to 2030, or approximately $790 million annually to 2063, to meet its investment needs, leaving an annual financing gap of $630 million (over K1.1 trillion).

a3724.speaker: Bertha Bangara Chikadza, Economics Association of Malawi president
a3724.name: Bertha Bangara Chikadza
a3724.title: Economics Association of Malawi president
a3724.speech: Said the country remains heavily dependent on foreign aid to finance its operations and bridge budget deficits: “This is why the withdrawal of the $350 million in [US Agency for International Development] funding created significant fiscal strain, demonstrating Malawi’s vulnerability.” ; added that Malawi’s economy remains structurally weak, with agriculture, employing about 80 percent of the population, contributing only 31 percent to GDP, leaving the economy vulnerable to climate-related shocks; said limited domestic revenue mobilisation and rising debt threaten investment in critical sectors and could hinder development progress.

a3771.speaker: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh, Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.name: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh
a3771.title: Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.speech: Vowed that if confirmed she will institute crucial measures for price control and stabilization to maintain economic stability and protect consumers from inflation and market volatility ; told Senators that under her watch the ministry will monitor the prices of essential commodities and implement regulatory measures to avoid price gouging, as well as coordinate with international partners and local suppliers to secure a stable supply chain so as to prevent shortages ; added that the enforcement of anti-profiteering laws to prevent unfair pricing practices, especially in basic goods such as rice, petroleum and building materials, will be among her key priorities ; noted that the Ministry will regularly conduct market surveys and assess economic data to adjust policies that safeguard against inflation.

a3771.speaker: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh, Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.name: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh
a3771.title: Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.speech: Pledged to create policies that encourage diversity in trade and reduce reliance on single-source imports, and at the same time support local producers to meet export standards and access international markets ; assured that the Ministry will open competition amongst importers to ensure better prices and quality of goods, and also establish trade partnerships and agreements that will position Liberian products in foreign markets, adding: "These strategies are intended to enhance Liberia's trade balance, generate foreign exchange and stimulate economic growth."

a3771.speaker: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh, Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.name: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh
a3771.title: Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.speech: On the issue of institutional capacity, committed to invest in continuous training and development programs to enhance employee skills, particularly in trade regulation, industrial policy and business support, as well as ensure that staffers have access to necessary resources, such as technology and data, to perform their roles effectively.

a3771.speaker: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh, Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.name: Magdalene Ellen Dagoseh
a3771.title: Liberian Commerce and Industry Minister-designate
a3771.speech: Commended former Minister Amin Modad for his roles at the Ministry and acknowledged that he established a series of plans with short and long-term targets aimed at achieving measurable progress, adding: "As we move forward, we are committed to carefully reviewing these plans, identifying the ones that align with our vision and mission and we are committed to implement those ones that offer greatest opportunities for success."

a3771.speaker: J. Alex Tyler, Bomi County Senator and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Commerce and Industry
a3771.name: J. Alex Tyler
a3771.title: Bomi County Senator and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Commerce and Industry
a3771.speech: Cautioned the nominee to work in unity for the greater good of the Ministry and the country's commerce, owing to her previous roles in government as an Assistant Minister ; ended the hearing by informing the nominee that the Committee members will revert to the committee room and subsequently report their findings and recommendations to the Senate Plenary for action.

a3972.speaker: Charles Artur, local official at the Episcopal Commission for Migrants, Refugees and Displaced Persons (CEMIRDE)
a3972.name: Charles Artur
a3972.title: local official at the Episcopal Commission for Migrants, Refugees and Displaced Persons (CEMIRDE)
a3972.speech: Says more and more victims of terrorism are arriving in and around the city of Nampula: “The situation continues to be serious. In addition to the displaced people who came from the province of Cabo Delgado, with the new situation that has occurred, we have ended up receiving a greater number of displaced people who are not yet registered” ; says one of the main problems for organisations that support the displaced is that they work almost in the dark, without knowing exactly how many people are going to arrive: “We can’t control the displaced people in our province, nor do we know where they are. The majority are families that gather in one place, and the authorities cannot determine whether they are displaced or not”.

a3972.speaker: Charles Artur, local official at the Episcopal Commission for Migrants, Refugees and Displaced Persons (CEMIRDE)
a3972.name: Charles Artur
a3972.title: local official at the Episcopal Commission for Migrants, Refugees and Displaced Persons (CEMIRDE)
a3972.speech: Says lack of logistical and financial means has made the work difficult: “Firstly, the assistance is psychological. We try to involve these people in the work of the Diocese itself and we also provide some humanitarian assistance, like food and straw mats” ; “There are cases in which young girls end up prostituting themselves order to bring something into their homes. We also recorded cases of children who, at the age of 16, are already married”.

a3972.speaker: World Vision
a3972.name: World Vision
a3972.speech: Told DW that many NGOs are on “standby” waiting for information from the government on “how” and “where” to intervene.

a3972.speaker: International Organisation for Migration (IOM)
a3972.name: International Organisation for Migration (IOM)
a3972.speech: Points out that more than 800,000 people have fled their homes because of the conflict.

a3972.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, President of Mozambique
a3972.name: Filipe Nyusi
a3972.title: President of Mozambique
a3972.speech: Said in early September: “It [terrorism] is there in Nampula province [after it started in Cabo Delgado province]; what is needed is to control it.”

a3972.speaker: Wilker Dias, researcher
a3972.name: Wilker Dias
a3972.title: researcher
a3972.speech: Says the head of state’s warning comes too late: “In my view, intelligence has been failing since the beginning of the conflict in Cabo Delgado, given how long these attacks have persisted. We have the Rwandan troops there, we had the warning in June that Memba would be attacked, but intelligence was unable to forestall it.”

a3972.speaker: Wilker Dias, researcher
a3972.name: Wilker Dias
a3972.title: researcher
a3972.speech: Understands that the insurgents want to confuse the authorities, dispersing and taking the violence to various strategic points: “This move by the terrorists [to Nampula province] serves to put a certain pressure on the capital city of Cabo Delgado [Pemba], where the companies are headquartered” ; believes one of the main objectives of the terrorists is to sabotage gas exploitation on the Coral Sul floating platform: “We have already had the sabotage of onshore gas exploration, and now we will have the sabotage of exploitation on the high seas. If we don’t put a security cordon around the area where the exploitation of Coral Sul will be centred [Afungi], we run this risk too.”

a4008.speaker: NDP6 (2025–2030) national development policy document
a4008.name: NDP6 (2025–2030) national development policy document
a4008.speech: Earmarks the mining sector, which contributes over 13% to GDP, as a key driver of economic transformation, job creation, and industrial development, and underscores the need to transition from primary extraction to value addition, beneficiation, and increased local participation.

a4008.speaker: NDP6 (2025–2030) national development policy document
a4008.name: NDP6 (2025–2030) national development policy document
a4008.speech: According to the policy document, the mining sector’s high GDP contribution is at odds with its low employment absorption rate of just 2.6%, largely due to its capital-intensive nature; “The intent is to transform the country into an upper-middle-income economy through high-quality growth and a diversified economy where manufacturing and services constitute a greater share”; key targets for 2030 include raising the national employment rate from 64% to 75%, increasing the contribution of secondary industries to GDP from 15.6% to 25%, and boosting Gross National Income per capita from US$4,280 to US$6,900, as well as increasing sectoral productivity and “leveraging green industrialisation” by using Namibia’s minerals in clean technology manufacturing.

a4008.speaker: Fitch Solutions, political risk consultancy
a4008.name: Fitch Solutions
a4008.title: political risk consultancy
a4008.speech: “A particularly poor electoral performance in November 2024 could also increase political pressure on Swapo to promote more local beneficiation in the mining industry and the nascent oil sector, including requirements for local employment and investment in local processing.”

a4079.speaker: Nana Addo (Akufo-Addo), former President of Ghana
a4079.name: Nana Addo (Akufo-Addo)
a4079.title: former President of Ghana
a4079.speech: Assured Ghanaians that "NPP has the men".

a4079.speaker: Paul Afoko, former NPP national chairman
a4079.name: Paul Afoko
a4079.title: former NPP national chairman
a4079.speech: When he was national chairman, he insisted that no parliamentary candidate would be imposed on a constituency.

a4079.speaker: H.E. J.A. Kufuor, former President of Ghana
a4079.name: H.E. J.A. Kufuor
a4079.title: former President of Ghana
a4079.speech: Openly instructed in 2004 that no parliamentary candidate would be imposed on a constituency.

a4079.speaker: Two prominent members of "the Institution" (NPP figures, unnamed)
a4079.name: Two prominent members of "the Institution" (NPP figures
a4079.title: unnamed)
a4079.speech: "As for you, you are always in the opposition" ; "You are not one of us, you are not on the list."

a4079.speaker: NPP leadership (on the Sarfo-Maafo committee report)
a4079.name: NPP leadership (on the Sarfo-Maafo committee report)
a4079.speech: "We were told, the findings were too explosive to reveal, so the report was kept under someone's bed."

a4079.speaker: Arthur Kennedy
a4079.name: Arthur Kennedy
a4079.speech: According to Arthur Kennedy, the Elephants led by the Elephas Maximus Borneensis "have gone back to the bush."

a4188.speaker: Ulaç Demirag, IFAD Country Director for Ethiopia
a4188.name: Ulaç Demirag
a4188.title: IFAD Country Director for Ethiopia
a4188.speech: “Access to finance is crucial for rural people – particularly those whose incomes are threatened by a changing climate – to expand their businesses, and to take advantage of new emerging livelihood opportunities along agricultural and agro-industrial value chain.” ; “This new programme will provide financial products and services to poor rural people in the least developed areas to promote poverty reduction and livelihood risk mitigation.”

a4204.speaker: 2025 Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC)
a4204.name: 2025 Global Report on Food Crises (GRFC)
a4204.speech: Revealed that at least 6.8 million Malawians — over one-third of the population — are unable to meet basic food needs, with 5.7 million people classified under IPC Phase 3, a category that signals severe acute food insecurity; warns that rising poverty and malnourishment are direct consequences of declining welfare, linking this to macroeconomic pressures including foreign exchange shortages, reduced official development assistance, and fragile fiscal capacity: “These factors threaten currency stability and Malawi’s ability to import essential goods.”

a4204.speaker: Preliminary crop production estimates for the 2024/25 season
a4204.name: Preliminary crop production estimates for the 2024/25 season
a4204.speech: Indicate that Malawi will harvest only 2.96 million metric tonnes of maize against a national requirement of 3.5 million, a shortfall of more than half a million metric tonnes.

a4204.speaker: Leonard Chimwaza, agriculture extension specialist
a4204.name: Leonard Chimwaza
a4204.title: agriculture extension specialist
a4204.speech: Has called for a shift from emergency responses to long-term strategies, recommending prioritizing mega farm productivity, timely input distribution, climate-smart farming, and improved storage infrastructure; stressed that government must diversify food sources through small-scale livestock farming, and that Admarc’s role in ensuring equitable and affordable maize distribution is crucial, especially in the short term.

a4204.speaker: Sam Kawale, Minister of Agriculture, Malawi
a4204.name: Sam Kawale
a4204.title: Minister of Agriculture, Malawi
a4204.speech: Acknowledged the gravity of the crisis but pointed to ongoing efforts, revealing that government is investing nearly K100 billion in irrigation projects, with support for fertiliser, seeds, and pest control aimed at boosting off-season production: “We are committed to ensuring no one is left behind. Dodma will continue distributing free food to vulnerable households, and Admarc has received additional funding to sell maize at subsidized prices.”

a4259.speaker: Divian Govender, Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.name: Divian Govender
a4259.title: Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.speech: "With this exclusive partnership, Cipla will have access to SII's current vaccine portfolio," told Health24.

a4259.speaker: Divian Govender, Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.name: Divian Govender
a4259.title: Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.speech: Said Cipla Medpro expects to be very competitive with their pricing of vaccines used by the Department of Health (DoH) in the Expanded Programme for Immunisation (EPI) ; "Cipla is committed to providing pharmaceuticals and vaccines at cost-effective prices, making quality medicines affordable, and advancing healthcare for all South Africans. We understand the burden on the country to supply affordable medicines and it is Cipla's firm intention to assist in this regard."

a4259.speaker: Divian Govender, Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.name: Divian Govender
a4259.title: Cipla's Chief Business Development Officer
a4259.speech: "Cipla was able to secure stock from SII and supply the DoH with the BCG vaccine via the Section 21 permit route," adding that a second order of the BCG vaccine was being processed.

a4259.speaker: Cipla Medpro (company statement)
a4259.name: Cipla Medpro (company statement)
a4259.speech: Noted that its partnership with the SII, which has a presence in 140 countries, will be instrumental in addressing the national vaccine shortage.

a4259.speaker: Michel Baijot, Cipla Ltd Head of Vaccines
a4259.name: Michel Baijot
a4259.title: Cipla Ltd Head of Vaccines
a4259.speech: "This Cipla Medpro SII agreement reflects again the complementarities of our two like-minded companies in bringing high quality, affordable vaccines to more countries."

a4259.speaker: Adar Poonawalla, Serum Institute of India CEO and Executive Director
a4259.name: Adar Poonawalla
a4259.title: Serum Institute of India CEO and Executive Director
a4259.speech: "We are confident that this agreement will support the DoH in rolling out its EPI."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: "It is a historic turning point. For more than two decades, Syrians endured a regime marked by repression, torture and indiscriminate bombardment. Bashar al-Assad used every possible means to stay in power: arbitrary imprisonment, massacres, use of chemical weapons... Today the Syrian people can finally hope for a different future."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: "It must be acknowledged that these rebels succeeded where others failed. They waged an intense struggle against a regime that seemed indestructible. But beyond the military victory, what matters is what comes next. We hope that this new force in power will not repeat the mistakes of the past and will work for the good of the Syrian people."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: On the priority challenges: "The first challenge is stability. Syria has been devastated by years of war and political instability. A framework must be put in place quickly to allow Syrians to live in security and rebuild their country. Then there is the economy: millions of people are displaced, infrastructure is destroyed, and famine threatens. Reconstruction will require colossal efforts. Finally, reconciliation: after so much suffering, the social fabric must be recreated and the country must be prevented from falling into a new spiral of violence."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: On fears that the rebel victory does not necessarily mean freedom: "It is a legitimate concern. The Syrian people did not fight to replace one oppression with another. Those who have taken power must understand that they bear a historic responsibility: they must not betray the aspirations of those who suffered and fought for a better future."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: On the role of the international community: "The international community must be a support, not a force of interference. Humanitarian aid and reconstruction will be essential, but they must be put in place with the Syrian people and for the Syrian people. We have seen in the past that ill-conceived foreign interventions can aggravate crises rather than resolve them."

a4355.speaker: Bachar Kateb, Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.name: Bachar Kateb
a4355.title: Honorary Consul of Syria
a4355.speech: A final word to Syrians hoping for a renewal: "I want to tell them that their courage was not in vain. The road will still be long, but they deserve a country where they can live with dignity, without fear or oppression. Today a new page is opening: it is up to them to write their future."

a4375.speaker: Maria Manuela Lucas, Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4375.name: Maria Manuela Lucas
a4375.title: Mozambican Minister of Foreign Affairs
a4375.speech: Claims that the country has not yet received any notification of the deportation of citizens in an irregular situation following the mass deportations under way in the United States, and that the Mozambican authorities are prepared to welcome and repatriate any of their citizens who may be deported ; “We haven’t received any notification. We must receive notification to know how many Mozambicans are going to be repatriated. We haven’t received that notification yet, so we don’t know how many Mozambicans are going to be repatriated, if they are deported”, she said.

a4398.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a4398.title: Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.speech: Gave a glowing account of Djibouti's policy of welcome and openness towards refugees and urged the international community to show greater solidarity in order to strengthen partnerships and humanitarian assistance so as to lighten the impact on the economic and social development of host countries.

a4398.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a4398.title: Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.speech: On the IGAD support platform, praised its merits, saying it "constitutes an important mechanism in the search for durable solutions for the refugees of our region and requires the support of all technical and financial partners in achieving its objectives" ; recalled IGAD member countries' commitment to accelerate implementation of costed national response plans supporting the Nairobi Declaration and Plan of Action ; stressed host countries' vulnerability: "the success and strengthening of our commitments remain largely dependent on the situation in our region, marked by recurrent conflicts and political turbulence that make the search for a durable solution for refugees difficult" ; regretted the continued disengagement of technical and financial partners and appealed to all international partners to strengthen support for the IGAD platform through predictable and multi-year funding ; reaffirmed his confidence in IGAD.

a4398.speaker: Said Nouh Hassan, Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.name: Said Nouh Hassan
a4398.title: Minister of the Interior of Djibouti
a4398.speech: On Sudan: "Djibouti deplores the humanitarian and security situation in Sudan, a brotherly country torn apart by a fratricidal conflict that has caused a heavy human toll, massive population displacement and the destruction of socio-economic infrastructure" ; "Faced with this crisis in Sudan, my country has always worked for the return of peace, stability and national unity... Djibouti reiterates its attachment to the rapid initiation of a ceasefire, an indispensable precondition for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the return of a peaceful, stable, single and indivisible Sudan" ; "President Guelleh believes that only a negotiated political solution will allow Sudan to emerge from the current crisis, and we reiterate our determination to work with all countries and organisations acting in this direction" ; "It is in this spirit that His Excellency Ismail Omar Guelleh and his government will continue to support regional (IGAD), continental (African Union) and multilateral peace initiatives, such as the Jeddah platform co-organised by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the United States, with IGAD's support."

a4563.speaker: Dr. Vamsi Krishna, managing director, Hetero Group of Companies
a4563.name: Dr. Vamsi Krishna
a4563.title: managing director, Hetero Group of Companies
a4563.speech: “Hetero is pleased to partner with the Gates Foundation to create a pathway for the sustainable and affordable supply of lenacapavir. This collaboration reflects our commitment to ensuring access to innovative HIV medicines for patients in India and other low- and middle-income countries.”

a4563.speaker: Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) and Wits RHI (announcement)
a4563.name: Unitaid
a4563.title: the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) and Wits RHI (announcement)
a4563.speech: Announced new commitments with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Ltd. (DRL), another Indian manufacturer, reinforcing efforts to build a competitive generics ecosystem.

a4563.speaker: Public health experts
a4563.name: Public health experts
a4563.speech: See lenacapavir for PrEP as a transformative option for people who face barriers to daily oral PrEP, including stigma, adherence challenges, and inconsistent access to medication.

a4563.speaker: Modeling / study cited
a4563.name: Modeling / study cited
a4563.speech: Modeling suggests that the introduction of lenacapavir has the potential to prevent significant numbers of HIV infections; one study showed that scaling up access to affordable lenacapavir to just 4% of the population in high-burden countries could prevent up to 20% of new infections.

a4563.speaker: Trevor Mundel, president of global health, Gates Foundation
a4563.name: Trevor Mundel
a4563.title: president of global health, Gates Foundation
a4563.speech: “Scientific advances like lenacapavir can help us end the HIV epidemic—if they are made accessible to people who can benefit from them the most. We are committed to ensuring that those at highest risk, who can least afford it, aren’t left behind.”

a4563.speaker: Bill Gates, Chair, Gates Foundation
a4563.name: Bill Gates
a4563.title: Chair, Gates Foundation
a4563.speech: Announced the foundation's $912 million pledge to the Global Fund's 2026-2028 replenishment fundraising campaign, which aims to save 23 million lives from HIV, malaria, and tuberculosis between 2027 and 2029 ; earlier this year announced he would give away virtually all of his wealth to the foundation and that the foundation would spend $200 billion over the next 20 years toward three primary goals: ending preventable deaths of moms and babies; ensuring the next generation grows up without deadly infectious diseases; and lifting millions of people out of poverty.

a4563.speaker: Kate Hampton, CEO, Children's Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF)
a4563.name: Kate Hampton
a4563.title: CEO, Children's Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF)
a4563.speech: “The deals announced today on generics are a major step forward in ending the HIV epidemic. They build on full value-chain investments by CIFF and others to foster a competitive market so that access to lenacapavir is affordable and reliable for all those who need it.”

a4593.speaker: Barbra Banda, Zambian footballer, CAF Women's African Player of the Year 2024
a4593.name: Barbra Banda
a4593.title: Zambian footballer, CAF Women's African Player of the Year 2024
a4593.speech: "I feel great, it is something I have been working hard for to be here," Banda is quoted as saying by CAFonline. "Last time round I did not win but this time I made it, which makes me feel great and amazing." ; At the winner's podium she said the secret to her exploits "is just training hard and paying attention to what you are doing" and offered advice to aspiring young women footballers "not to look down on themselves but to keep working hard and be determined and disciplined [as] hard work always pays off".

a4593.speaker: Ademola Lookman, Nigerian footballer, CAF Men's African Player of the Year 2024
a4593.name: Ademola Lookman
a4593.title: Nigerian footballer, CAF Men's African Player of the Year 2024
a4593.speech: "It is an incredible achievement and an incredible moment," Lookman said at the winner's podium. "It is special to join a list of many great players who have achieved a lot in the game. They are legends. There are a lot of special moments that happened this year, I can speak about a lot of good moments. But also the bad moments, when you don't want to do gym, but you end up doing that session and that gives you more strength. The difficult moments have given me that extra strength. For us to be able to give inspiration to the young kids who want to be like us is the most important thing. If we can set a good example, they have good footsteps to follow."

a4637.speaker: Namibian Ministry of International Relations
a4637.name: Namibian Ministry of International Relations
a4637.speech: Announced that the Namibian government has nominated the Cuban Medical Brigade for the 2021 Nobel Peace Prize.

a4637.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, Namibian Minister of International Relations
a4637.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a4637.title: Namibian Minister of International Relations
a4637.speech: Said the nomination is rooted in the recognition of the brigade's extensive work of exporting Cuba's medical skills for the benefit of communities across the world; said Cabinet affirmed its support for the nomination of the brigade for the prize, and that her ministry last December fulfilled all requirements of the Norwegian Nobel Committee and submitted the nomination.

a4637.speaker: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, Namibian Minister of International Relations
a4637.name: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah
a4637.title: Namibian Minister of International Relations
a4637.speech: "While the brigade has been extensively involved in providing support to countries across the world since the beginning of the Covid-19 pandemic, the work around fighting global pandemics is not new to the brigade" ; said the brigade also worked to combat Ebola in West Africa in 2014 and had focused support for the people of Haiti when they experienced a cholera epidemic in 2010 ; "Namibia recognises this as a consistent commitment to acknowledging health as a fundamental right and providing support in emergency situations with full appreciation for the risks humanitarian crises pose to peace and development" ; "Cuba has displayed global citizenship par excellence by espousing international solidarity despite the economic and financial embargo which severely constrains the country and this makes the brigade worthy of Namibia's nomination."

a4646.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a4646.name: Experts (unnamed)
a4646.speech: have warned that the lives of nearly two million Nigerians living with HIV are in danger unless the Federal Government immediately takes over funding for HIV services and ends donor reliance ; said the trend was a clear signal for Nigeria to take over the services.

a4646.speaker: UNAIDS (Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS)
a4646.name: UNAIDS (Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS)
a4646.speech: According to UNAIDS, the country has the world’s fourth highest HIV burden ; the HIV prevalence among adults aged 15 to 49 is estimated to be 2.1 percent.

a4646.speaker: NACA (National Agency for the Control of AIDS)
a4646.name: NACA (National Agency for the Control of AIDS)
a4646.speech: According to NACA, approximately 90% [of the 1.9 million people in Nigeria who had HIV as of 2021] were receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART).

a4646.speaker: Dr. Chinonso Egemba (‘Aproko Doctor’), physician and health commentator
a4646.name: Dr. Chinonso Egemba (‘Aproko Doctor’)
a4646.title: physician and health commentator
a4646.speech: expressed concern about the poor condition of Primary Health Care (PHC) centres in Nigeria, taking netizens on a video tour of one of such PHCs. He emphasised the critical need for relevant stakeholders to prioritise investments in these centres, emphasising that healthcare begins at the grassroots. He stated that strengthening PHC facilities is critical for improving access to quality care, particularly in underserved communities, as well as addressing the country’s fundamental health challenges.

a4646.speaker: Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN)
a4646.name: Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim
a4646.title: President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN)
a4646.speech: “The first thing that made us aware of this type of thing was Coronavirus. Many countries halted drug exports during the Coronavirus pandemic. For example, India prohibits the export of drugs. They say they intend to use it for their people. African countries realised they were on their own. Following the Coronavirus, many African governments began to think ahead. In our country, we realised that we do not reproduce APIs (active pharmaceutical ingredients); you now need to add excipients to manufacture drugs.” ; “In fact, many companies have begun; I believe Emzor Pharmaceutical is among them. Jawa only launched the Beta Lactam plant about two months ago. Many companies are establishing API plants, and we will soon have enough API manufactured in Nigeria to eliminate our reliance on ‘oyibos’ for our drug needs.”

a4646.speaker: Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN)
a4646.name: Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim
a4646.title: President of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN)
a4646.speech: “Fortunately, there was an outcry even in the United States about what President Trump has done, that many people will die because they cannot afford to buy those drugs, and that he has reversed himself on certain aspects of the law. So, the ban on all things affecting HIV, drugs, tuberculosis, drugs, and everything has been lifted, and the drugs will continue to be provided for free.”

a4646.speaker: Pharm. Ambrose I. Eze, National Chairman of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN)
a4646.name: Pharm. Ambrose I. Eze
a4646.title: National Chairman of the Association of Community Pharmacists of Nigeria (ACPN)
a4646.speech: believes the aid cut scare is a wake-up call for Nigeria. “HIV medication is quite expensive. Despite funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), some people still lack access to the drugs. Lack of access to HIV drugs would cause an increase in infection, raising HIV prevalence rates. HIV drugs will become prohibitively expensive due to a lack of access and availability. Therefore, US President Donald Trump’s recent fund withdrawal directive is a strong signal that African countries like Nigeria must begin to look inward and take over the funding of essential healthcare services from donors. The government should take over the funding of essential healthcare services, which is currently driven by donors. As a result, public-spirited individuals, private-sector organisations, and bodies in Nigeria should all support the government’s initiatives. In addition, public-spirited individuals, private sector organisations, and bodies can take over funding for special healthcare services in their communities.”

a4646.speaker: Richard M. Mills Jr., US Ambassador to Nigeria
a4646.name: Richard M. Mills Jr.
a4646.title: US Ambassador to Nigeria
a4646.speech: clarified the current status of US assistance to Nigeria, stating that the new administration has implemented a 90-day pause to review and improve the effectiveness of the assistance. Mills emphasised that no assistance has been cut, and no decisions have been made regarding the future of US assistance to Nigeria. “Let me clarify one point. Right now, the new administration has put a 90-day hold on our assistance. No assistance has been cut, and no decisions have been made regarding the future of our assistance. In fact, Secretary Rubio has stated that this does not mean ending foreign assistance to our partners and friends, such as Nigeria. It is about how to make the assistance more effective and ensure that it is consistent with US government policies and interests. So that is the purpose of this 90-day pause, as well as our assistance. But, as many of you have seen, I hope there are waivers for our life-saving assistance, whether it is to HIV patients, mothers and children in need of nutrition, or internally displaced people. So if this continues, we will know where we will be in 90 days.”

a4646.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (cited by Ambassador Mills)
a4646.name: Marco Rubio
a4646.title: US Secretary of State (cited by Ambassador Mills)
a4646.speech: has stated that this does not mean ending foreign assistance to our partners and friends, such as Nigeria. It is about how to make the assistance more effective and ensure that it is consistent with US government policies and interests.

a4646.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4646.name: Temitope Ilori
a4646.title: Director-General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a4646.speech: stated that while the waiver provides immediate relief, Nigeria remains cautious about potential future changes in US foreign aid policies. She emphasised the importance of strengthening local funding and stakeholder collaboration to ensure HIV treatment remains accessible to those in need, regardless of shifts in international donations.

a4667.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4667.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.speech: Told the media after the Cabinet meeting on Tuesday that Cabinet had adopted the proposed Industrial Reconstruction and Growth Plan after a presentation by Industry and Commerce Minister Mangaliso Ndhlovu, who chairs the Cabinet Committee on Industrialisation and Export Development ; said measures will be implemented to promote electronic transactions and the development of the Small to Medium Enterprises Formalisation Strategy as the use of Point of Sale (POS) machines will become compulsory for all businesses ; said the Plan will also focus on improving the ease of doing business, enhancing government and private sector collaboration while considering developments in Bilateral and Multilateral engagements such as the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Southern African Development Community (SADC), and the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA).

a4667.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4667.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.speech: On manufacturing growth: “Major focus to promote growth of the manufacturing sector will be on import substitution, manufacturing of raw materials for the manufacturing industry, utilisation of idle manufacturing assets, the local content strategy implementation, value chain optimisation, rural industrialisation, export development, research and innovation for industrial development, and financing for manufacturing” ; “Stock-taking of idle infrastructure will be conducted with a view to legally and procedurally make them available to potential investors and businesses in need of operating space. The revitalisation of bus and truck manufacturing initiatives in the country will serve to unlock more funding.” ; said priority will be given to institutionalisation of the Buy Zimbabwe Campaign, harmonization of standards and establishment of specifications in promoting the public procurement of locally available goods, adding that an incentive structure for companies procuring and supporting the local industry in an upward ratio of 70:30 for local versus imports will be developed and operationalised ; “The Plan will foster and facilitate linkages in all sectors through backward and forward linkages.”

a4667.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4667.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.speech: On rural industrialisation: “Key enablers to the implementation of the rural industrialization drive includes identification of land for the development of industrial parks, identification of competitive and comparative advantage resource endowments and industrial projects in rural districts, setting up an Inter-Ministerial Committee on Rural Industrialisation which will periodically update Cabinet on progress”; said rural industrialization will take on board automation of existing industries to enhance competitiveness, and establishment of hubs across the country including within farming areas with a view of creating markets for agricultural products.

a4667.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4667.title: Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister of Zimbabwe
a4667.speech: On financing: “To address challenges with access to affordable long-term financing, an array of options will be utilised including equity financing, private and government funding” ; “The Industrial Development Corporation of Zimbabwe (IDCZ) will enhance its role as a development finance institution. Additional funding sources will also be pursued, including working with the multilateral finance institutions. Efforts will be made to nurture and improve the environment for the participation of the private sector funding mechanisms.”

a4734.speaker: Mikhail Zvinchuk, @rybar project manager (video summary for @SolovievLive)
a4734.name: Mikhail Zvinchuk
a4734.title: @rybar project manager (video summary for @SolovievLive)
a4734.speech: Said the West is preparing a conference on Sudan without the participation of the authorities in Khartoum, with rebel allies from the RBU, including Kenya and the UAE, invited while Moscow and Tehran are not: "All this speaks to the West's policy of legitimizing the militants and trying to create an alternative government" ; said the United States and France are betting on Morocco as the West's main outpost in Africa ; said the escalation between Mali and Algeria is connected with the hiding place of militants and separatists on Algerian territory.

a4734.speaker: Washington (US government)
a4734.name: Washington (US government)
a4734.speech: Has reaffirmed its support for Moroccan autonomy in Western Sahara, which excludes its independence.

a4734.speaker: Sudanese Ambassador
a4734.name: Sudanese Ambassador
a4734.speech: Protested the West's planned conference on Sudan held without the participation of the authorities in Khartoum.

a4734.speaker: Mali (government)
a4734.name: Mali (government)
a4734.speech: Accused Algeria of complicity in terrorism after the incident with the downed drone; the Sahel Alliance ambassadors have been recalled from Algeria.

a4797.speaker: Lee Roussel, Resident Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4797.name: Lee Roussel
a4797.title: Resident Director of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4797.speech: Stressed: “This success will come if and only if the customs administration effectively supports this effort.” ; “Operators’ choices of ports are very sensitive to even a small difference in security, in formal and informal fees, and in the hours it takes to move goods through.” ; She indicated that the customs administration as well as the Port are urgently called upon to initiate the necessary reforms, and specified that customs clearance in Cotonou must be faster and cheaper; failing that, she fears, the billions invested in modernizing the Port of Cotonou would bring very little to the Beninese people, and even the enormous infrastructure being built will not prevent ships from increasingly abandoning the Port of Cotonou in favour of competing ports. For her, modernizing customs is imperative to truly accelerate the growth of Benin’s economy.

a4867.speaker: Save the Children (UK-based charity)
a4867.name: Save the Children (UK-based charity)
a4867.speech: Said on Wednesday that eight people in South Sudan, including five children, died on a three-hour walk to seek medical treatment for cholera after U.S. aid cuts forced local health services to close; the organisation said in a statement that it supported 27 health facilities in eastern South Sudan's Jonglei State until earlier this year when the U.S. cuts forced seven to shut completely and 20 to close partially.

a4867.speaker: Christopher Nyamandi, Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
a4867.name: Christopher Nyamandi
a4867.title: Save the Children's country director in South Sudan
a4867.speech: "There should be global moral outrage that the decisions made by powerful people in other countries have led to child deaths in just a matter of weeks."

a4867.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a4867.name: Donald Trump
a4867.title: U.S. President
a4867.speech: Said the cuts imposed after entering office on January 20 were to ensure grants were aligned with his "America First" agenda.

a4867.speaker: Experts
a4867.name: Experts
a4867.speech: Have warned that the cuts - including the cancellation of more than 90% of USAID's contracts - could cost millions of lives in the coming years due to malnutrition, AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and other diseases.

a4867.speaker: U.S. State Department (spokesperson)
a4867.name: U.S. State Department (spokesperson)
a4867.speech: Said it did not have information about the deaths reported by Save the Children; a spokesperson said many U.S. government programmes providing lifesaving aid in South Sudan remained active but that support for medical services had also been used to enrich the country's leaders: "While emergency lifesaving programmes continue, we will not, in good conscience, ask the American taxpayer to provide assistance that effectively subsidises the irresponsible and corrupt behaviour of South Sudan's political leaders."

a4867.speaker: South Sudan's government
a4867.name: South Sudan's government
a4867.speech: Has in the past acknowledged a significant amount of public corruption but denied specific accusations of graft, including against President Salva Kiir's family.

a4940.speaker: George Conway, UN Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a4940.name: George Conway
a4940.title: UN Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a4940.speech: called on all parties to protect civilians and humanitarian workers in the country's conflict areas; said the country has recorded 124 incidents affecting humanitarian access in 2024, with 12 aid workers injured and 13 incidents of physical assault, harassment, and intimidation.

a4940.speaker: George Conway, UN Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
a4940.name: George Conway
a4940.title: UN Deputy Special Representative of the Secretary-General, Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator for Somalia
